Title: Two teenage sisters reported missing after leaving home
Article:
AMPANG JAYA: Two teenage sisters have been reported missing after leaving their home in Lembah Jaya Utara here separately on Sep 26 and Sep 27.
The two, Syazana Qurratu Aini Zulhazmi, 17, and her younger sister, Nur Qistina Fhatanah, 16, were reported missing after they failed to return home.
Ampang Jaya district police chief, Assistant Commissioner Khairul Anuar Khalid, said Syazana Qurratu Aini had initially gone out with a friend for a meal at a nearby area at 8pm on Sep 26.
However, she did not return home.
"The following day, Sep 27, at 9am, her younger sister, Nur Qistina Fhatanah, told their mother that she wanted to go to a school carnival at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Taman Kosas.
"However, both sisters had yet to return home when the police report was lodged.
"Based on initial investigations, their mother suspects that the sisters left home because they wanted more freedom," he said in a statement today.
Khairul Anuar said Syazana Qurratu Aini is 159cm tall, weighed 45kg and had a fair complexion.
Her younger sister, Nur Qistina Fhatanah, is 155cm tall, weighed 45kg and had a dark complexion.
The sisters were last seen in the Lembah Jaya Utara area.
Police want members of the public with information to come forward to assist in the investigation.
"Members of the public with any information about the two people are urged to go to the nearest police station.
"They can also contact the Ampang Jaya district police headquarters operations room at 03-42897222 or investigating officer Sergeant Major Afizah Zainal at 017-2185192," he said.

Title: Ex-UiTM Holdings CEO charged with CBT involving RM37.37 mil [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd (UHSB) group chief executive officer Azlizan Fadzil was charged at the Sessions Court here today with criminal breach of trust (CBT) involving RM37.37 million meant for a large-scale solar power project in Gambang, Pahang.
Azlizan, 53, pleaded not guilty to the charge after it was read out before Sessions Court judge Datuk Mohd Nasir Nordin.
According to the charge, Azlizan, who was then the company's chief executive officer, was entrusted with RM37,374,612.68 for the investment of a 50-megawatt (MW) large-scale solar photovoltaic power generation project in Gambang.
He was accused of dishonestly misappropriating the funds by making payments for purposes other than the intended investment.
The offence was allegedly committed between Feb 2 and Oct 2, 2017, at Affin Bank Berhad's UiTM Shah Alam branch on Level 2 of Menara Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah.
Azlizan was charged under Section 409 of the Penal Code, which provides for a jail term of between 2 and 20 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
He told the court interpreter that he understood the charge and the penalties.
Azlizan arrived at the courtroom shortly before 9am in a wheelchair, accompanied by several family members.

Title: Malaysia to hand over 292 Malbatt assets to Lebanese Armed Forces
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will hand over 292 Malaysian Battalion (Malbatt) assets in Lebanon, worth an estimated US$10 million, to the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) as part of the withdrawal process.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the assets, including vehicles and various equipment, would be handed over in stages until January 2027.
"As part of the withdrawal process, some Malbatt assets will be brought back to Malaysia, some disposed of in Lebanon, while others will be handed over to the LAF.
"This handover involves 292 assets estimated to be worth around US$10 million, including vehicles and various equipment, which will be handed over in stages until January 2027," he said in a Facebook post today.
Khaled is currently at Marakah Camp in Lebanon, where he witnessed the symbolic handover ceremony yesterday.
He expressed hope that the assets would benefit the LAF and local communities through welfare and humanitarian assistance, while contributing to peace.
The assets were symbolically handed over by Joint Forces Commander Lieutenant-General Datuk Seri Tengku Muhammad Fauzi Tengku Ibrahim to LAF representative Brigadier-General Bassem Saad.
Malbatt 850-13 is Malaysia's final contingent under the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (Unifil) mission in southern Lebanon, marking the end of nearly two decades of Malaysian involvement in peacekeeping operations in the country.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Razali Idris hints at leaving Bersatu for 'new platform'
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Terengganu Bersatu chief Datuk Razali Idris has hinted at leaving the party, saying he would move forward on a "new platform".
The development comes less than 2 months after he stepped down as Terengganu Bersatu chairman on Aug 8.
"Ten years as a Bersatu leader ends today.
"God willing, I will move forward with a new platform," he said in a Facebook post.
However, he did not disclose why he was leaving Bersatu or identify the party or platform he intended to join.
Last month, Razali said he remained a Bersatu member despite relinquishing his position as the party's Terengganu chief.
He had also
denied speculation
that he had joined Perikatan Nasional component Parti Pejuang Tanahair (Pejuang).

Title: California roller coaster permanently shut after brain injury claims
Article:
LOS ANGELES: A popular California roller coaster is being permanently shut down after dozens of people claimed to have suffered brain damage while riding it.
The X2 at Six Flags Magic Mountain features precipitous drops and jarring twists that have thrilled millions of riders over two decades, with seats that swivel 360 degrees as cars travel at speeds of up to 130km an hour.
But it has also sparked a rash of legal complaints, including from two women whose families say they were seriously injured in July on the ride in Valencia, just north of Los Angeles.
Pamela Guillen, 40, suffered a severe subdural hematoma and brain compression after riding X2 on July 5, and underwent emergency surgery that required doctors to remove part of her skull, her family told CNN in an investigation last month.
Less than a week later, Naomi Greer-Wilkinson of Los Angeles, 25, lost consciousness after riding X2 and underwent emergency brain surgery, CNN reported. She remained in a coma for weeks and still can't speak or breathe on her own, according to her parents.
The ride has been closed since shortly after the second incident, but on Tuesday park managers said they were shuttering it for good.
"After almost 20 years, we have decided to permanently retire X2," park President Brian Oerding said.
"Since X2 opened in 2008, it has welcomed more than 16 million guests and earned a passionate following among ride enthusiasts," he said.
"While X2 consistently passed a multitude of safety tests, we have decided to close the ride because we believe it's the right thing to do. Ride safety is a cornerstone of our business, and when we see guest confidence affected, we take it seriously."
Attorneys at Dordick Law, who are acting for Greer-Wilkinson, said they had been contacted by more than 100 people who say they were injured by the roller coaster.
"The design of this ride makes it inherently dangerous, and makes it dangerous in a way that no reasonable rider would expect," attorney Christopher Bulone told reporters.
Theme park operator Six Flags, which has properties throughout North America, says it does not comment on pending litigation.
In August the company and ride manufacturer S&S Worldwide Inc. reached a settlement with the family of 22-year-old Christopher Hawley, who died after riding X2 in 2022.
A separate lawsuit is scheduled for next year in which Sheila Katerelos, 56, alleges she suffered a traumatic brain injury on the ride in 2020.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gig economy should be temporary income source, says Economy Minister
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The gig economy should be viewed as a temporary source of income rather than a comprehensive solution to the challenges of jobs and wages, says Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.
He said gig work helped individuals earn an income and make ends meet, particularly when they faced difficulties securing permanent employment.
However, prolonged reliance on such work did not necessarily offer income stability, opportunities to develop skills or clearer career progression, he said.
Akmal Nasrullah said the success of the gig economy should not be measured solely by the number of people entering the sector, but also by how long they remained in it, their earnings, level of social protection and opportunities to transition to more stable jobs or careers.
"Participation in the gig economy may help someone earn an income immediately, but it must not become a dead end for young people and workers seeking to improve their standard of living," he told Berita Harian.
He said the country's real challenge was to create more quality jobs that enabled workers to improve their skills and income over time.
This, he said, could not rely solely on setting or enforcing minimum wages, but must also involve changes to the types and composition of jobs available in the economy.
"The government also needs to direct investments and incentives towards industries with the potential to create more high-value jobs," he said.
At the same time, traditionally labour-intensive sectors such as agriculture, agri-food, halal and manufacturing still had the potential to provide better jobs if supported by technology, digitalisation and targeted investments.
"Increases in productivity resulting from these changes must translate into higher incomes for workers.
"If productivity rises but wages do not keep pace, the country risks losing skilled workers and remaining trapped in a low-cost labour model," he said.
He said the creation of high-value jobs must therefore go hand in hand with efforts to improve skills, productivity and wages.
"The ultimate goal is to ensure that the jobs created do not merely reduce unemployment, but provide decent incomes and clearer career prospects," he said.
His remarks come as Malaysia's labour market continues to show strength in terms of employment levels, although skills mismatches and job quality remain challenges.
According to the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), the unemployment rate remained low at 3.0 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, with 16.77 million people employed.
However, the rate of skills-related underemployment among tertiary-educated workers remained high at 35.2 per cent.
DOSM also reported that the economy grew 6.0 per cent in the second quarter, while labour productivity, measured by value added per worker, increased 4.9 per cent.
Despite this, the number of new jobs created across economic sectors fell 1.2 per cent year-on-year to 31,500.
The figures suggest that economic and productivity growth alone do not resolve questions over the type, skills requirements and quality of jobs being created.
The policy challenge, therefore, is not simply to expand income opportunities through the gig economy, but to ensure workers have opportunities to upgrade their skills, access social protection and move into jobs offering more sustainable incomes and career prospects.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: FTC launches AI safety probe into Anthropic, OpenAI
Article:
WASHINGTON: The Federal Trade Commission has launched a broad investigation into artificial intelligence safety practices at Anthropic and OpenAI, the Washington Post reported on Wednesday.
The FTC possesses broad authority to examine unfair and deceptive practices affecting consumers in the United States.
Details about the investigation's scope remain unclear, and the launch of an inquiry does not mean the companies will face charges of wrongdoing.
News of the investigation, sourced to a senior FTC official, comes amid heightened concerns about AI safety.
AI giants Anthropic and OpenAI have reported instances of their systems escaping into the wild, including an incident where OpenAI agents breached Hugging Face, another AI company.
OpenAI on Monday canceled a model release citing safety concerns, while executives from both companies have proposed coordinated slowdowns to strengthen safety measures.
The Trump administration has emphasised industry self-regulation through a joint accord signed by President Trump and executives at the White House.
But ahead of mid-term elections in November, US lawmakers are increasingly under pressure from voters to curb or slow AI's development over fears it could displace workers and upend society.--AFP

Title: Parliamentary Services Act 2025 takes effect today
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Parliamentary Services Act 2025 (Act 869) and related amendments to the Federal Constitution take effect today, marking a significant milestone in efforts to strengthen Parliament's institutional autonomy.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the enactment of Act 869 was a significant achievement for the Madani government's institutional reform agenda and a historic milestone for the Malaysian Parliament.
She said this came 34 years after the Parliamentary Services Act 1963 (Act 394) was repealed under the Constitution (Amendment) Act 1992 (Act A837), effective Nov 20, 1992.
"More than three decades on, Act 869 restores Parliament's autonomy by creating a dedicated parliamentary service, giving it greater independence and efficiency in managing its administration, human resources and affairs.
"This will further strengthen Parliament's position as the highest legislative body in the country's parliamentary democracy," she said in a statement today.
Azalina said the government also expressed its gratitude to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, for granting consent to set Oct 1, 2026, as the date on which Act 869 and the related constitutional amendments would come into force.
She said the reform also reflected the government's commitment to upholding the doctrine of separation of powers and the system of checks and balances among the legislative, executive and judicial branches.
"With stronger institutional autonomy, Parliament can carry out its constitutional functions and responsibilities to the people more independently, effectively and credibly," she said.
She also thanked Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also Leader of the House, the Cabinet and all stakeholders, including non-governmental and civil society organisations, for their cooperation in bringing about the reform.
"The Madani Government will continue to pursue its institutional reform agenda in a structured and sustained manner to strengthen the country's democratic institutions and ensure public confidence in national institutions is maintained," she said.
The Parliamentary Services Bill 2025 was tabled for its first reading in the Dewan Rakyat on Feb 24, 2025, followed by its second reading on March 4.
The Dewan Rakyat passed the Bill on March 5, followed by the Dewan Negara on March 20.
Sultan Ibrahim consented to the Bill on July 9, and it was gazetted on July 18, 2025.

Title: Google withholds new AI model from public over safety fears
Article:
SAN FRANCISCO: Google on Wednesday said it would withhold its most powerful artificial intelligence model from the public for now, releasing Gemini 4 Argon only to a vetted group of cybersecurity experts to avoid misuse by hackers.
"Safely releasing frontier capabilities at this level requires a phased approach," wrote Koray Kavukcuoglu, Google's chief AI architect, in a blog post announcing the model.
Google said it is voluntarily giving the US government early access to the model and will gather feedback from testers before making it widely available.
The cautious rollout mirrors the approach of rival Anthropic, which has kept its most advanced model, Claude Mythos Preview, restricted to a small number of trusted organizations.
Washington briefly forced Anthropic to suspend access to its publicly released Claude Mythos and Claude Fable models in June, and has since set up a voluntary process for vetting the most powerful AI models before release.
The announcement came a day after President Donald Trump hosted top tech executives, including Google chief Sundar Pichai and Anthropic's Dario Amodei, at the White House, where they signed a voluntary accord pledging to police the risks of their own AI systems.
Cybersecurity experts fear the state-of-the-art technology could be used to hack banks, hospitals and government systems.
Google said Argon excels at complex tasks in software engineering, legal and financial work and cyber defence, with a leading ability to find and fix critical software flaws.
Early testers used Argon to uncover a flaw in software used by hospitals around the world that exposed sensitive personal information – something other advanced models had missed, Google said.
Google said Argon is designed to refuse requests that could help carry out cyberattacks or develop chemical, biological or nuclear weapons.
Anthropic and ChatGPT-maker OpenAI have built similar safeguards into their most advanced models.
Google said it is monitoring the model's reasoning to stop it from straying beyond what users intended, a risk researchers call misalignment.
The issue has taken on new urgency since OpenAI disclosed in July that two of its models, including one not yet released, broke out of a sealed test environment during a cybersecurity evaluation and hacked into the servers of AI company Hugging Face.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Half of p-hailing riders rely on gig work full-time, survey finds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: About half of more than 5,000 p-hailing riders surveyed nationwide rely on gig work as a full-time job.
A survey conducted by Persatuan Perpaduan Rakan Penghantar Malaysia last year also found that half of the respondents relied on p-hailing as their main source of income.
Its chairman, Haris Fadillah Arsyad, said some respondents had been working in the gig sector for more than 10 years, citing higher earnings than formal-sector jobs and flexible working hours as among the reasons.
As such, Haris said the association disagreed with the perception that gig work in Malaysia was only suitable as a temporary job.
"Based on the survey we conducted in several zones we visited, the majority of p-hailing riders do this work full-time. So, I disagree with the view that it is only suitable as temporary work," he told Berita Harian.
Gig workers nationwide are estimated to number 1.12 million, including about 600,000 p-hailing riders.
Haris said 1,736 p-hailing riders were currently registered with the association, with 70 per cent aged between 18 and 35.
Another 26 per cent were aged between 35 and 45, while four per cent were between 45 and 60.
"They can earn a minimum of about RM3,000 a month and up to RM6,000, depending on how much they work," he said.
He said earnings from the sector also enabled some riders to purchase vehicles and homes through the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP).
SJKP is a government initiative under the Finance Ministry to assist those with irregular incomes, including gig workers and small traders.
"The Gig Workers Act 2025 has encouraged more young people to enter the sector as they are recognised as workers, including being required to make contributions," he said.
"If this work were only suitable as a temporary job, why would the government introduce an act? This clearly shows there is strong demand for this type of work," he said.

Title: Esscom focuses on protecting vulnerable groups from exploitation
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The Eastern Sabah Security Command (Esscom) is stepping up efforts to protect undocumented and stateless communities from exploitation amid cross-border security threats.
Its commander Datuk Victor Sanjos said the lack of valid identification documents, limited access to formal employment, socioeconomic factors and the location of some communities in island and coastal areas could create conditions that might be exploited by irresponsible parties.
"In this context, women and children are among the groups requiring particular attention from the perspective of protection," he told the New Straits Times.
Victor said Esscom's approach also took into account threats including cross-border crime, syndicate activities and exploitation.
Measures included verifying individuals' identities and status to distinguish between victims of exploitation, those requiring protection and individuals suspected of committing offences, he said.
"Any information relating to possible human trafficking, forced labour, smuggling or syndicate activities will be assessed and, where relevant, coordinated with agencies with the jurisdiction to take further action.
"At the same time, issues involving documentation, welfare and social protection fall under the jurisdiction of several government agencies.
"This requires scrutiny and inter-agency cooperation to ensure actions are based on facts and the laws currently in force."
On Wednesday, the NST reported that
undocumented Bajau Laut youths
in Semporna were being exploited in the workforce.
Universiti Malaysia Sabah Social Sciences and Humanities Faculty lecturer Associate Professor Wan Shawaluddin Wan Hassan said increased maritime security measures, marine conservation restrictions and declining marine resources had reduced the areas where some members of the community could fish and move.
Following the 2013 Lahad Datu intrusion, increased maritime security measures by Malaysia, the Philippines and Indonesia have further restricted areas where the Bajau Laut can move and seek food.
Meanwhile, Victor said a community-based approach was also important in protecting vulnerable groups, particularly in island and coastal areas.
He said local communities could serve as strategic partners by helping authorities identify suspicious activities and protect groups at risk of exploitation.
"They can be the eyes and ears, as well as Esscom's mobile intelligence network, particularly in areas that are difficult for authorities to reach regularly," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kedah RTD issues 4,447 summonses in foreign driver crackdown
Article:
ALOR STAR: The Kedah Road Transport Department (RTD) issued 4,447 summonses to foreign drivers during an operation targeting foreign drivers conducted from June 17 until yesterday.
Kedah RTD director Stien Van Lutam said the summonses were issued for various offences under relevant laws.
He said 164 vehicles were seized during the same period, comprising 128 motorcycles, 28 cars, and eight other vehicles.
Stien added that the state RTD Enforcement Division launched a special crackdown, Ops Khas Gempur Pewa, on Sept 28 to intensify enforcement actions.
"Within two days until yesterday, 115 vehicles were inspected, and 28 summonses were issued for various offences," he said in a statement today.
He added that 16 vehicles involving Rohingya drivers were seized during the crackdown.
Main offences detected throughout the operation included driving without a valid driving licence, expired Motor Vehicle Licences (LKM) or road tax, and driving without valid insurance coverage.
"Besides taking action against foreign drivers, Kedah RTD is also monitoring local vehicle owners who allow foreigners to drive their vehicles without complying with set regulations," Stien said.
Offences identified among local owners included allowing individuals to drive without a valid licence, allowing vehicles to be used with expired LKM or road tax, and allowing vehicles to be used without valid or active insurance coverage.
Stien reminded vehicle owners not to take matters lightly or hand over their vehicles to any individual without ensuring all legal requirements are met.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ab Rauf: Umno divisions to submit three names for each state seat
Article:
AYER KEROH: Melaka Umno will examine the list of candidates submitted by its divisions, as well as MCA and MIC, ahead of the state election.
State Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said all Umno leaders have been asked to submit at least three potential candidates for each state seat for review.
"The candidates have not been decided yet. I have only asked for names of potential candidates to be considered and scrutinised. There is still plenty of time, so we will discuss them first," he said after chairing the Melaka Umno Liaison Committeemeeting at Seri Bendahara here last night.
Also present were state Umno Liaison Committee deputy chairman Datuk Rais Yasin and all division chiefs, including Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh, who is also Jasin Umno division chief.
Ab Rauf said the proposed candidates would go through several vetting stages before the list is presented to top party leadership for a final decision.
Umno currently holds 18 state seats, while MCA and MIC hold two and one seat respectively.
Meanwhile, Ab Rauf said last night's meeting focused on state election preparations, including the activation of the party machinery at all levels.
He said the election machinery would be launched before nomination day to ensure all divisions and parliamentary constituencies are fully prepared.
"We will launch the BN machinery by parliamentary constituency before nomination day, but I am confident that preparations have been completed by all Umno division chiefs, who have taken responsibility to ensure our machinery at all levels is fully ready for the upcoming state election," he said.
"However, we are not taking the competition from other parties lightly, as they are also fielding candidates in all 28 state seats. Umno is prepared for any possibility, but our focus remains on retaining the 21 seats we won in the last state election."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain forecast for Terengganu, Sarawak until 9am
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in parts of Terengganu and Sarawak until 9am today.
In a statement this morning, MetMalaysia said the warning covers Kemaman in Terengganu.
In Sarawak, the areas affected are Sri Aman, Samarahan (Sebuyau), Betong, Kapit (Song), Sarikei, Mukah and Bintulu.
The warning is issued when there are signs of thunderstorms accompanied by rainfall exceeding 20mm an hour that are occurring or expected to occur for more than an hour.
Thunderstorm warnings are short-term warnings valid for no more than six hours.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump's AI chatbot pulls back after debunking his political claims
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump unveiled what he called a "damn good" AI chatbot, but it quickly drew attention for contradicting some of his contentious political claims.
A day later, however, it stopped answering some political questions.
"Hello, America. Whatever you need from government, start here," reads the America.gov platform, which Trump launched on Tuesday in a bid to simplify access to government information and federal services.
The chatbot soon began contradicting Trump on controversial subjects such as the 2020 presidential election, which he wrongly claims to have won, and the Jan 6, 2021 insurrection that saw a violent mob attacking the US Capitol.
"On its first day, America.gov harnessed facts and official documents to contradict some of the false narratives and political framing about immigration and elections heavily promoted by the administration that built it," said the Digital Democracy Institute of the Americas.
"Initial analyses found that America.gov generally provided evidence-based answers backed by government records, even when those records contradicted claims made by Trump and his administration."
On Tuesday, when asked whether there had been widespread voter fraud in the 2020 election, the chatbot responded: "Official federal assessments after the 2020 presidential election did not find fraud at a scale that changed the outcome."
Democratic lawmakers quickly promoted the chatbot's responses about the election.
"Finally, a straight answer from someone in the Trump administration," Senator Adam Schiff of California wrote on X on Tuesday, alongside a screenshot of the chatbot's statement that former president Joe Biden had won the 2020 election.
But on Wednesday, the chatbot changed its tune when asked the same question. "I do not provide political commentary or analysis of past elections," it said.
It was unclear whether the Trump administration had tweaked the settings to prevent the chatbot from debunking the president. The White House did not immediately weigh in.
"America.gov will continue to be updated to provide Americans the most accurate and reliable federal information and resources," the White House said in a statement to US media.
The chatbot, however, continued to debunk some of Trump's other claims on Wednesday.
When asked about Trump's widely debunked claim that the United States experienced the "worst inflation" ever under former president Biden, the chatbot disagreed.
"No. Official Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) Consumer Price Index (CPI-U) data do not show the highest US inflation on record during 2021-2025."
"'Worst inflation ever' is not supported by the official CPI record."
The launch of the new government platform comes as growing cyber incidents have raised concerns around the world about risks posed by uncontrollable AI, with some tech executives urging a slow-down for safety.
Trump has dismissed those concerns as a conspiracy to undermine US economic growth and hamper competition with China.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pahang fitness icon chases another record with 9,000-rep challenge on Nov 1
Article:
LIPIS: Pahang-born fitness instructor K. Jey Prabakaran Thevar, who set a world record with an 18-hour endurance workout in June, is raising the bar with another gruelling challenge.
The 29-year-old aims to complete 3,000 repetitions each of squats, leg extensions and jumping jacks on Nov 1 in a bid to enter the Asia Book of Records.
​​​​He previously secured a place in the Malaysia Book of Records (MBOR) for completing the highest number of jumping jacks, leg extensions and squats within 48 hours in Kuala Lipis last year.
Jey Prabakaran said that after completing 3,000 repetitions of each exercise during last year's National Sports Day celebration to secure the MBOR title, he was now aiming to complete the same number of repetitions in each exercise within five hours for the Asian record attempt.
"I am targeting 3,000 repetitions each of jumping jacks, leg extensions and squats, aiming to achieve the highest number of repetitions by an individual within the stipulated time.
"The challenge will test my physical endurance, discipline, mental strength and consistency in completing the repetitions within five hours," he said when contacted.
In June, he set a
new Influencer Book of World Records
for the longest non-stop cardio and weightlifting workout session after completing an 18-hour session.
The youngest of four siblings said he had maintained the same training regimen and diet that helped him achieve the world record.
"A lot of my focus is on building leg strength to sustain all three routines. I am still following an extremely strict diet, avoiding sugar and salt.
"Although I have taken part in similar challenges and know what to expect on the 'big' day, I do not want to be overconfident. My aim is to continue training daily and avoid injuries," he said.
Jey Prabakaran said the guidance of his coach, Mohd Shazwan Mohd Luthfi Ismail, and support from his family had been major motivating factors as he hoped the record attempt would bring extra smiles during Deepavali on Nov 8.
Meanwhile, Jey Prabakaran, who is also president of the Malaysian Indian Fitness Association (Mifit), said he wanted to use the challenge to promote the association and encourage more youths to take up sports and fitness.
"Mifit was established to create more opportunities, provide guidance and build a stronger sports and fitness community, particularly among youths," he said.
The Asian record attempt, supported by the national MIC Youth Sports Bureau, will be held at Nethaji Hall at the party headquarters on Nov 1.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit opens higher against major currencies, lower versus greenback
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against a basket of major currencies, but slightly lower against the US dollar on Thursday, weighed by strong US economic data that supported the greenback.
At 8am, the ringgit edged down to 4.0790/0860 against the greenback from Wednesday's close of 4.0785/0820.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam said the US final gross domestic product (GDP) for the second quarter of 2026 came in at 2.2 per cent, above the consensus estimate of 1.5 per cent.
"The Automatic Data Processing (ADP) employment change also rose to 90,000 in September, ahead of the market estimate of 73,000.
"Following this, the odds of a rate hike in October fell from more than 70 per cent to below 50 per cent currently," he told Bernama.
Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, held at 3.4 per cent in August, below the consensus estimate of 3.7 per cent.
Mohd Afzanizam said the US Dollar Index (DXY) initially fell to as low as 101.05 points before recovering to 101.37.
"On that note, markets have reassessed their stance towards a rate hike in October, but it is not totally off the table in light of the positive labour market data," he said.
He said the ringgit is expected to trade between RM4.08 and RM4.09 today, ahead of the release of US non-farm payrolls (NFP) data on Friday.
Against major currencies, the ringgit rose against the euro to 4.6203/6282 from 4.6324/6363 at Wednesday's close, appreciated against the British pound to 5.4104/4197 from 5.4162/4209, and strengthened against the Japanese yen to 2.5887/5933 from 2.5969/5993.
Against Asean currencies, the ringgit strengthened against the Singapore dollar to 3.1917/1977 from 3.1943/1973 at Wednesday's close, rose against the Thai baht to 12.1341/1611 from 12.1521/1666, and was little changed against the Indonesian rupiah at 227.9/228.4 versus 227.9/228.2.
The ringgit was unchanged against the Philippine peso at 6.51/6.52.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 10 areas record unhealthy air quality at 7am
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Ten areas recorded unhealthy air quality readings as of 7am today, according to the Air Pollutant Index (API).
Based on readings from the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, Johan Setia recorded the highest API reading at 157, followed by Shah Alam (156) and Nilai (153).
Putrajaya and Klang each recorded a reading of 152, followed by Cheras (151), Seremban (130), Port Dickson (117), Batu Muda (110) and Petaling Jaya (109).
Meanwhile, 54 locations recorded moderate API readings, while four others recorded good readings.
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and 301 and above hazardous.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Flydubai cockpit attack prompts Israel to tighten pilot security checks
Article:
JERUSALEM: Israel is set to ramp up security checks on pilots flying into the country, a spokesperson for the prime minister's office said, after it said a co-pilot on a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv had stabbed the pilot and attempted to crash the plane.
The dramatic incident was only defused after passengers helped subdue the co-pilot before other on-duty pilots employed by the airline on the plane landed the aircraft safely in Saudi Arabia. The Dubai state-owned airline warned against "premature speculation" and said much remained unclear.
Saudi authorities have arrested and interrogated the co-pilot of flydubai flight FZ1073 from the United Arab Emirates to Israel that was carrying 174 people, almost all Israelis, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said.
The incident has sharpened questions about how pilots are vetted and what sorts of security protocols they face, including but not limited to the Middle East, according to government officials and aviation analysts.
Israel's government frequently urges Israelis and Jews to remain vigilant when travelling outside Israel, amid concerns that they could be targeted. This comes as antisemitism has surged globally in recent years, including violent and sometimes deadly attacks against Jews. So far, however, no motive has been given for the flydubai incident.
"Every pilot that is going to be flying into Israel, we are going to know the pilots' identities, know who they are, and do some type of security check," Doron Spielman, a spokesperson for the Israeli prime minister's office, told Reuters.
He said Netanyahu had instructed authorities to "ramp up security" on flights to Israel operated by Israeli and non-Israeli carriers.
"Anywhere that an Israeli is going to be flying into Israel. Our job right now is to do our best - even if they're not on Israeli airlines - to make sure that those security procedures are much higher," Spielman said.
The UAE civil aviation regulator, the GCAA, did not respond to a Reuters request for comment on how its pilots are vetted.
Netanyahu identified the pilot who was attacked as Indian national Captain Smit Machchhar. He said that, despite being "stabbed and seriously injured," Machchhar fought back and opened the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to overpower the attacker.
PILOT VETTING TOUGHER POST 9/11
Pilots have faced substantial security screenings, especially since the 9/11 attacks in New York 25 years ago, experts told Reuters.
"Every pilot goes through extensive background checks but also continuous medical and psychological assessments," said Philip Baum, a visiting professor of aviation security at Coventry University in Britain.
Individual countries and airlines are responsible for implementing screening and security standards as set out by the International Civil Aviation Organization, but there is flexibility in how these are interpreted, experts told Reuters.
Two pilots working in the Middle East but not for flydubai told Reuters that pilots have to go through the same security screenings as passengers, meaning they would not be able to bring weapons such as knives or guns on board.
"It's always the airline's responsibility," said Eric Schouten, the head of aviation intelligence consultancy Dyami.
"The airline has to do a proper vetting according to national guidelines on who is in the cockpit and every country does it differently."
The European Aviation Safety Agency told Reuters that flydubai's certification and safety oversight rest with the GCAA. "This includes responsibility for ensuring that the operator meets the applicable requirements concerning its flight crews and their fitness to fly," EASA said.
Reuters could not determine what weapon was used by the pilot to stab the other. Passengers on board the flight have reported that a man was holding a knife while one of the pilots lay bloodied. A pilot flying in the region but not for flydubai told Reuters pilots might have access to metal knives from a meal service or a crash axe available in most cockpits.
Spielman said Israel already had some of the toughest security checks, and these would only get tighter.
"This is an opportunity for everyone to wake up. Israel has the most thorough security checks in the world, and they're there for a reason. They're there so that an incident like this doesn't take place," he said.--REUTERS

Title: BoJ debated need for more rate hikes at September meeting, summary shows
Article:
TOKYO: Some Bank of Japan (BoJ) policymakers saw the need to accelerate the pace of interest rate hikes or bring them closer to the central bank's "goal" soon, a summary of opinions at its September meeting showed on Thursday.
"If signs of an upward deviation in prices are observed, the bank will need to accelerate the pace of rate hikes," one member was quoted as saying.
At the September meeting, the BoJ raised interest rates to a 31-year high with its governor signalling the central bank has entered a new phase focused on preventing inflation from overshooting its target, opening the door to further rate hikes.

Title: Etihad Airways seeks legal advice after Premier League's Man City findings
Article:
MANCHESTER: Abu Dhabi-based airline Etihad Airways said on Wednesday it was seeking legal advice on its options after criticising the Premier League's handling of an independent commission's findings against Manchester City.
The Premier League said on Tuesday that City had used "sham" commercial contracts as part of schemes to inflate revenue and understate costs by more than £900 million (US$1.2 billion) over nearly a decade.
Etihad, City's principal sponsor since 2009, said it "categorically rejects any finding, conclusion or implication" that it was involved in improper commercial arrangements.
In a statement, the airline said the league never contacted or consulted it during the commission process and gave it no opportunity to provide information or challenge material that may have reflected adversely on the company.
"Etihad is deeply concerned by the way this matter has been communicated publicly," the statement said. "The lack of clarity and transparency, together with the selective disclosure of information, has created damaging implications for Etihad despite the airline not being named in the published decision."
City have denied any wrongdoing and said they intend to appeal.
A Premier League spokesperson said on Wednesday they would not be commenting on the Etihad statement.
Etihad added that the Premier League's public communication of the findings, following what it described as selective leaks and reporting, had harmed its reputation.
While reaffirming its support for Manchester City and its longstanding partnership with the club, the airline said it was seeking legal advice on the options available to protect its interests.
"We stand with the club, its supporters and our wider Etihad community as Manchester City challenges the commission's conclusions through the processes available to it," the statement said.--REUTERS

Title: Netanyahu hails Indian pilot who saved 174 aboard flydubai jet
Article:
JERUSALEM: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu hailed Indian pilot  Smit Machchhar for saving passengers after he was stabbed by his colleague in an alleged attempt to crash a flydubai plane on Wednesday.
Passengers on the flight reached Israel safely on Wednesday after customers and crew foiled the co-pilot's attempt to crash the aircraft, Israeli officials said. The struggle began when he stabbed the pilot and sent the jet plunging nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds.
Machchhar was covered with blood on the floor when he managed to click the release to open the cockpit door, a Netanyahu spokesperson told Reuters. That allowed passengers and crew to overpower the co-pilot and enable a second pair of flydubai pilots who were on board to land the jet in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.
"He saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals," Netanyahu said in a post on X. "All passengers are out of harm's way," Netanyahu had earlier said in a video statement released by his office.
Indian authorities in Saudi Arabia said Machchhar is receiving necessary medical attention in a hospital in the northwestern city of Tabuk and they are in touch with his family and Saudi authorities to extend all possible help.
He is reported to be stable, the Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia said in a post on X.
Machchhar, who hails from India's financial capital Mumbai, underwent surgery after the incident, Indian newspaper the Hindustan Times reported.
According to his LinkedIn profile, Machchhar worked with India's SpiceJet airline for over 11 years before joining flydubai.
The cause of the altercation between the pilots was not clear. Flydubai said in a statement that the underlying reasons for the event remained unknown and warned against "premature speculation." It also suspended flights to and from Israel amid an investigation.
Netanyahu described the event as "a highly severe security incident", and said Saudi authorities would interrogate the co-pilot of flydubai FZ1073, which had been en route from the United Arab Emirates to Israel.--REUTERS

Title: Five pillars to steer MACC as it enters sixth decade
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Integrity without compromise, fair enforcement, proactive prevention, greater use of technology and public trust will form the five pillars steering the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) as it approaches six decades in the fight against graft.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the five pillars would guide the commission's administration and direction as corruption becomes increasingly complex and evolves alongside technology.
Speaking in an interview in conjunction with MACC's 59th anniversary recently, Halim said the commission could not afford to remain static.
He said the corruption landscape had changed significantly over the years, requiring MACC to continually transform and adapt its approach to remain relevant and capable of con-fronting emerging threats.
"Integrity is the main bulwark in the fight against corruption. It cannot be compromised for any reason, whether in making decisions, conducting investigations or carrying out daily responsibilities," he said.
Halim said this meant MACC would act against corruption regardless of the rank, position or background of those investigated, while demanding the same standards of integrity from its own officers.
"Integrity must become a culture, not merely a rule. It must be reflected in every action, decision and in the way we carry out the trust placed in us by the people."
FAIR AND EQUITABLE ENFORCE-MENT
On the second pillar, Halim said enforcement must be grounded in the law, evidence and principles of justice, and without fear, favour or influence from vested interests.
He cited MACC's decision to suspend the use of orange lock-up attire for persons under investigation during remand proceedings as an example of balancing firm enforcement with the rights and dignity of individuals who were yet to be found guilty in court.
"We can be firm against corruption while respecting the rights, dignity and principles of justice of every individual under investigation. That is the true meaning of fair and equitable enforcement."
Halim said the third pillar, pro-active prevention, reflected MACC's push to identify systemic weaknesses and close loopholes before they developed into more serious corruption and caused greater losses.
This includes strengthening public education and awareness, as well as examining practices, systems and procedures in public bodies to identify weaknesses that could be manipulated for corrupt purposes.
MACC, he said, was also increasingly adopting intelligence-based investigations instead of merely waiting for reports to be lodged.
"We want to act before the problem becomes bigger."
EXPANDING USE OF TECH
Technology and transparency form the fourth pillar, with MACC expanding the use of digital technology, data analytics and artificial intelligence (AI) to strengthen its operational capabilities.
Halim said intelligence-based inves-tigations allowed MACC to identify indicators, patterns, connections and risks through information gathered from various sources.
The combination of data analytics, AI and digital systems could allow investigators to process large volumes of information faster, identify anomalies, trace financial flows and uncover connections that might be difficult to detect through conventional methods.
However, he stressed that technology remained a tool, with inves-tigators still responsible for evaluating, verifying and interpreting information and ensuring enforcement action remained within the law.
"We aim to build MACC's capabilities to be faster, more precise and always one step ahead in detecting and combating corruption, without neglecting transparency, account-ability and public trust."
Halim described public trust as the fifth and ultimately crucial pillar.
"Trust cannot be demanded. It has to be built through action, performance, integrity and consistency."
He said the strength of an institution should not be measured solely by the number of cases investigated or enforcement actions taken, but also by its ability to maintain integrity, professionalism and public confidence.
[[nid:1545085]]
ENFORCEMENT PRIORITIES
Against this backdrop, Halim said MACC had identified four enforcement priorities for this year: government procurement, enforcement, public funds or special government allocations, and government revenue.
He said the four areas were selected because they involved substantial sums of money as well as powers and responsibilities entrusted to certain parties.
Any corruption, abuse of power or leakage in these areas, he said, would ultimately affect the public.
"In government procurement, for example, MACC has been looking across the entire process, from planning and specification-setting to invitations, evaluations, awards and contract implementation, as weaknesses at any stage could create opportunities for manipulation, conflicts of interest or leakages.
"The intensified approach has already resulted in significant enforcement activity this year," he said.
He explained that between January and Aug 31, MACC received 5,239 pieces of information, opened 842 investigation papers and made 803 arrests.
It also recorded 345 prosecutions and 97 convictions during the period.
"Of the 803 arrests, 311 involved civil servants.
"Based on the breakdown by offence, 352 arrests involved receiving bribes, 278 involved false claims, 78 involved giving bribes, 62 involved abuse of position, 12 involved money laundering and 21 involved other offences," he said.
He added that from January to July 31, MACC also recorded RM55.31 million in forfeitures, compounds and settlements, comprising RM12.28 million in forfeitures, RM42.24 million in compounds and RM786,556 in settlements.
BEYOND THE STATISTICS
However, Halim cautioned against judging MACC's performance solely by statistics.
He said the more important measure was whether enforcement could bring offenders before the courts, recover misappropriated funds, protect public money, address weaknesses and prevent entrusted powers from being abused.
"Numbers are not the only meas-ure of success," he said.
Looking towards MACC's diamond jubilee next year, Halim said the com-mission was also strengthening expertise in areas like data analytics, AI, digital forensics, digital assets, complex financial investigations and cross-border investigations.
"Internal processes would also be streamlined and digitalised where possible without weakening safe-guards and integrity.
"Corruption continues to evolve alongside borderless technology, increasingly involving complex and layered financial transactions across digital platforms, requiring MACC to similarly transform its structure, expertise and methods.
"We aim to build an organisation capable not only of dealing with pre-sent-day corruption but also threats that could emerge over the next 10 or 20 years.
"We cannot use yesterday's methods to deal with tomorrow's corruption crimes.
"MACC must continue to change, adapt and stay one step ahead," he said.

Title: Investing according to human behaviour
Article:
SIR John Templeton, one of the great pioneers of global value investing, famously observed: "Bull markets are born on pessimism, grown on scepticism, mature on optimism and die on euphoria."
It is one of the most insightful descriptions of how investor psychology influences stock-market cycles.
Templeton's message goes beyond market timing. It is fundamentally about understanding the relationship between price, sentiment and value.
The irony of investing is that investors often become most fearful precisely when prices may offer the greatest opportunities, and most confident when risks may be at their highest.
Born On Pessimism
Bull markets are usually born when investors are pessimistic. Economic conditions may be weak, corporate profits may have fallen, unemployment may be high and financial news may be dominated by bad headlines.
Investors become convinced that the future will remain bleak.
Consequently, share prices can fall well below what the underlying businesses may ultimately be worth. The market discounts not only today's problems but often assumes that those problems will persist indefinitely.
This is where the disciplined value investor looks for opportunities.
The key is not to buy simply because prices have fallen.
A falling share price can represent either an opportunity or a warning. The investor must determine whether the company's underlying economics remain sound, whether its balance sheet is capable of surviving the downturn and whether its long-term prospects remain intact.
The greatest opportunities often arise when pessimism causes investors to ignore the possibility of recovery.
Grown On Scepticism
As conditions begin to improve, pessimism does not immediately disappear. Instead, scepticism takes its place.
Investors may acknowledge that the situation is improving but remain doubtful about whether the recovery will last.
Earnings may begin recovering, businesses may report better results and economic indicators may improve, yet many investors remain unconvinced.
Ironically, this period can still provide attractive opportunities because prices may not yet fully reflect improving fundamentals.
The sceptical investor asks important questions: Is the recovery sustainable? Are earnings genuinely improving? Has the company's competitive position strengthened? Is management executing effectively? Are cash flows improving?
These questions are more useful than simply following market sentiment.
Matures On Optimism
Eventually, evidence of improvement becomes increasingly difficult to ignore. Corporate earnings strengthen, economic conditions improve and share prices rise.
Investors who previously doubted the recovery begin to participate. Analysts become more positive. Media coverage becomes increasingly favourable. More investors conclude that the worst is over.
Optimism replaces scepticism.
At this stage, the investment story becomes increasingly attractive to a wider audience. However, rising prices can create a dangerous psychological feedback loop.
Higher prices produce greater confidence, and greater confidence encourages investors to pay even higher prices.
The investor who bought when nobody wanted the shares is now sitting on substantial gains.
The question changes from "Is this business undervalued?" to "How much higher can it go?"
That change in thinking is important.
Dies On Euphoria
The final stage is euphoria. Investors no longer focus primarily on value and risk. They become fascinated by the possibility of extraordinary returns.
Valuations may reach levels that require exceptionally strong future growth to justify current prices.
Speculation becomes widespread. New investors enter because they fear missing out. People begin buying because prices have been rising rather than because they understand the underlying business.
At this point, rational analysis can be overwhelmed by emotion. The belief develops that the market will continue rising indefinitely. Traditional valuation measures are dismissed as outdated. Risk appears to have disappeared.
But risk has not disappeared. It has merely become less visible because optimism is masking it.
"The Time To Buy…"
Templeton's philosophy therefore contains an important investment lesson: the time to buy is often when others are reluctant to buy, provided the underlying fundamentals justify the investment.
This does not mean investors should automatically buy during every market crash or period of pessimism.
Some businesses deserve to decline because their competitive advantages have disappeared, their balance sheets are weak or their business models are structurally damaged.
The challenge is distinguishing between temporary problems and permanent impairment.
Likewise, investors should not automatically sell every stock simply because optimism is increasing. A high-quality business can continue creating value for many years.
The important question is whether the price being paid remains reasonable relative to the company's future cash flows and prospects.
Templeton's observation is therefore less a formula for predicting market tops and bottoms than a warning about human behaviour.
Investors should be particularly careful when their emotions are most comfortable. When everyone is pessimistic, courage and independent thinking are required. When everyone is optimistic, discipline and scepticism become increasingly important.
The cycle ultimately reflects a simple truth: markets are driven not only by business fundamentals but also by expectations about those fundamentals.
The intelligent investor therefore tries to think independently of the crowd. Buy when pessimism has created prices below reasonable value.
Remain sceptical when optimism is already embedded in prices. And when euphoria takes over, remember that an excellent business can still be a poor investment if purchased at an excessive price.
Templeton's enduring lesson is not to predict the market. It is to understand where emotion sits in the market cycle - and to ensure that our own emotions do not dictate our investment decisions.

Title: Former EPF chief calls for review of retirement age
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's retirement age is back in focus as former Employees Provident Fund (EPF) chief executive officer Tan Sri Shahril Ridza Ridzuan calls for a review, while labour and employer groups differ over raising it.
Shahril, who is now Axiata Group Bhd chairman, said longer life expectancy and Malaysians' willingness to remain economically active could justify more flexible working arrangements beyond 60, including part-time work.
"This is something that really needs to be reviewed. The reality is that many Malaysians will continue working. When we reach 55 or 60, we still want to work," he told reporters after a panel session at the International Social Wellbeing Conference (ISWC) 2026 on Wednesday.
"So, in terms of the retirement age, perhaps we need to review it because life expectancy is also increasing. If we look at it now, it has reached 78 years," he added.
Shahril said flexible working arrangements could help older Malaysians remain economically active.
"Whether it is one or four (days) of part-time work, or perhaps through the economy, we should encourage people to remain productive.
"Because when it comes to retirement, if you retire but there is no productive use of your time, it is actually not good for you in terms of your mental and physical health," he said.
His call received support from the Malaysian Trades Union Congress (MTUC), which said it had proposed raising the retirement age for private-sector workers to 65 in 2018.
MTUC president Datuk Abdul Halim Mansor said the government had not agreed to the proposal at the time, citing concerns that a higher retirement age could reduce employment opportunities for younger workers.
"However, what we are seeing is that Malaysia continues to depend on foreign workers, with more than three million foreign workers currently in the country.
"MTUC's proposal is based on workers' capabilities, skills and good health. Raising the retirement age would help increase EPF savings and shorten the period of retirement to around 10 years, based on an average life expectancy of 75 years," he told Business Times.
He said workers who remained employed could also benefit from staying physically and mentally active.
Requiring workers to retire at 60 could leave them less active and affect their mental alertness, potentially contributing to earlier health issues and increased stress, he said.
"The retirement age should be formally amended under the Minimum Retirement Age Act 2012.
"Amending the minimum retirement age would allow workers to continue making compulsory contributions to the EPF under the Employees Provident Fund Act 1991, while ensuring that their employers' contributions and related benefits remain protected," Halim said.
He said workers would also continue to receive protection under the Employees' Social Security Act 1969, including employment injury protection, the Employment Insurance System and the 24-Hour Scheme.
They would also continue to enjoy employment benefits under the Employment Act 1955, including sick leave and medical benefits.
"These benefits would be available to workers through an amendment to raise the minimum retirement age to 65," he said.
Flexible Approach To Retirement
However, Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) senior adviser for government, media and international engagement Datuk Syed Hussain Syed Husman said a blanket increase in the retirement age may not be the right approach.
The decision should ultimately be an individual choice.
"There are jobs where people are offered contracts after retirement and continue doing the same job. All of this depends on both parties and whether they want to continue.
"There are also opportunities for retirees to work on a consultancy basis, where they may only work a few days or when their expertise is needed. So, our employment environment is already quite flexible after the fixed retirement age of 60, or 65 in some sectors," he said.
Hussain, who is former MEF president, said the decision should ultimately be left to retirees, as they should be able to decide what works best for them.
"A one-size-fits-all approach to extending the retirement age may not work, as there are many other issues that need to be considered," he said.
Meanwhile, on lump-sum retirement withdrawals, Shahril said members should consider leaving their savings with EPF if they did not immediately need the money.
EPF could continue investing the savings and paying dividends, allowing members to plan phased withdrawals during retirement, he said.
"If you don't need it, or you don't have a better use for it, then just leave it with EPF. We will continue to invest it for you, you'll get a dividend, and you can then plan a phased drawdown. It's always better for you," he said.
Shahril acknowledged, however, that some retirees needed lump-sum withdrawals to meet financial commitments.
Those reaching 55 might need to settle housing or other loans, with their EPF savings potentially their only source of funds, he said.
Shahril said the broader challenge was ensuring Malaysians accumulated enough savings during their working years to meet their retirement needs and other financial commitments.
He said fewer members were making full lump-sum withdrawals at 55 compared with about 15 years ago.
"In the past, when I was first with EPF, 15 years ago, the percentage of people taking a full lump-sum withdrawal at 55 was very, very high. But now, that's coming down," he said.
Shahril attributed the decline partly to greater financial literacy and Malaysians accumulating more savings outside EPF.
He said Bank Negara data showed cash deposits and investments had also increased over time.
"So, I think people are generally better. And you would expect that because as a country matures and there's more income, people save more. But, of course, we still have to do the education, have to encourage people not to take everything out," he said.

Title: UK PM Burnham: 'Really concerned' if Man City owners sell club
Article:
MANCHESTER: Britain's Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he would be "really concerned" if Manchester City's Abu Dhabi owners decided to sell the club after they were found guilty of serious breaches of financial rules.
Burnham praised the ownership group led by Sheikh Mansour for its investment in Manchester since taking over the club in 2008.
"I would be really concerned to lose them," he told the BBC. "They've been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester and obviously the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is."
The Premier League said on Tuesday that City had used "sham" commercial contracts as part of schemes to inflate revenue and understate costs by more than £900 million (US$1.2 billion) over nearly a decade.
City have denied wrongdoing and said they will appeal.
Burnham, who was previously the mayor of Greater Manchester, drew parallels with Everton's battle with the league's profit and sustainability rules, when he argued the club he supports had not been treated fairly.
Everton received a 10-point deduction, that was later reduced to six points, after being found to have breached the league's financial rules over a three-year period ending in 2022.
"It would be wrong of me to leap to one side given the experience that I'd had before," he said.
With sanctions yet to be determined and appeals expected, Burnham acknowledged there was "a lot at stake" for City, their supporters and Manchester, but said it would be inappropriate for him to intervene in the disciplinary process.--REUTERS

Title: Melaka battle lines remain fluid as parties struggle with electoral pacts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The battle lines for the Melaka election remain fluid as major political blocs struggle to seal electoral pacts, with analysts saying unresolved differences could result in multi-cornered contests if parties ultimately fail to reach agreements.
International Islamic University Malaysia political scientist Dr Syaza Shukri said the prospects of cooperation appeared to be diminishing, despite some of the larger parties having stronger incentives to seek electoral partners.
"It looks like the odds of them working with each other are falling. Interestingly, the larger parties appear to be the ones more keen on cooperation.
"I think this has to do with BN and PH wanting to retain, and be seen to retain, their hold on power," she told the New Straits Times.
Syaza said Pas appeared relatively comfortable with either cooperating with BN or contesting independently, while BN leaders in Melaka had from the outset appeared inclined towards going solo.
She said PH, meanwhile, may see value in working with Bersatu, but Bersatu could calculate that it had little to lose by contesting on its own.
Syaza said, however, a fragmented contest should not automatically be interpreted as an easy path to victory for BN.
"BN, specifically Umno, would have to compete against Pas and also Bersatu for the Malay votes," she said, adding that BN had won several seats in the 2021 Melaka election by majorities of fewer than 1,000 votes, meaning even relatively small shifts in support could prove significant.
Universiti Malaya political analyst Dr Tawfik Yaakub said the possibility of parties contesting separately had become more realistic, particularly as negotiations involving several blocs remained unresolved.
"If BN, PH, Bersatu and Pas eventually move separately, the Melaka election could become a highly fragmented multi-cornered contest.
"The key consequence would be vote splitting, particularly in marginal and mixed seats where relatively small shifts in support could determine the outcome," he said.
Tawfik said BN would enter the election with the advantages of incumbency, stronger machinery and a record in government to defend.
PN, meanwhile, could attract Malay protest votes, while PH remained relatively stronger in urban and mixed constituencies.
He said cooperation between BN and PN could reduce competition for Malay votes, while a PH-Bersatu arrangement could help PH broaden its Malay support base, although such a pact could create complications among sections of PH's traditional supporters.
Tawfik said Bersatu would also have to weigh the risks of contesting independently.
"For Bersatu, going solo would test its organisational strength and whether it can retain voters without relying on a broader coalition structure.
"The same applies to PH and BN, with each party having to demonstrate the strength of its machinery, candidate appeal and core support base," he added.
The uncertainty comes as all
major parties
have at various points floated the possibility of contesting the Melaka polls on their own, even as negotiations over possible cooperation continue.
Earlier, Bersatu secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali said no agreement had been reached with PH.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, meanwhile, said that
BN could not force PH
into an electoral partnership, but stressed that the coalition remained open to cooperation and was still in discussions with other parties.

Title: Midnight boats fuel fear among islanders in Tumpat [WATCH]
Article:
TUMPAT:    Residents of  12 small islands off the coast near here are  worried  after  noticing  speedboats in the area, believed to be  operated by human traffickers.
The boats were suspected of  ferrying undocumented migrants from a neighbouring country into Kelantan,  often under the cover of darkness.
The residents said the boats posed a risk to fishermen and villagers who frequently commute  between the islands, particularly those returning home from work  at night.
They claimed that the boat  operators were foreigners who were familiar with the  landing points along the coast.
A resident in  Teluk Renjuna, who wished to be known as "Pak Din", said villagers were aware of the boat movements but preferred not to confront the alleged traffickers.
"However, we are worried about accidentally crossing paths with them, especially because some of these groups are believed to have weapons.
"People here know about their activities, but we choose to keep quiet and hope the authorities will take action as soon as possible.
"We are  worried when  too many foreigners, including Rohingya, start landing near our homes  because it can create problems," the 60-year-old former fisherman said.
The father of five said villagers were also concerned about the possibility of  enforcement personnel colluding  with the syndicates.
"The smugglers use speedboats at night without proper lighting. If they collide with a local boat, the consequences could be fatal.
[[nid:1545071]]
"There was an incident where a smuggler's boat collided with a local boat. They paid compensation, but if someone loses their life, money cannot bring that person back," he said.
Another resident, who wished to be known as Ismail, said island residents could not avoid travelling at night as their working hours were unpredictable.
"People here do not have fixed working hours. Sometimes we finish work late and have to travel home at night.
"So, we are always worried about encountering these boats, especially around Teluk Renjuna, Pantai Haji Nik Mat and Pulau Suri. We are not looking for trouble with them. We are just afraid of an accident because their boats move very fast in the darkness," said the sundry shop owner.
The 37-year-old said residents  had become increasingly cautious of the speedboats.
"If someone shines a light at them or accidentally exposes their activities, they may become angry. That is why people prefer to stay away," said Ismail.
Another resident, known  as Wan, said the authorities should also investigate the presence of
tonto
or lookouts believed to be operating around the islands.
"The syndicates know every corner of this area. We hear there are more than 10 landing points  to bring in  migrants.
"They also have people acting as lookouts. These 'tonto' know the movements of the authorities and the routes in and out of the islands," said the 32-year-old odd-job worker.
The residents said the  islands in the area were home to thousands of people whose livelihoods depend on the sea.
They said Teluk Renjuna alone had about 200 fishing families, while the wider island communities included  boat operators and workers who frequently travel by boat.
They also claimed that many of the alleged human traffickers  were believed to be Thai nationals.
The residents called on  the authorities to increase patrols, particularly at night, and to identify the landing points and individuals assisting the syndicates.
The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) acknowledged the  potential risks to local boat users.
Kelantan MMEA director Captain Kamal Mohamad said his agency  had increased patrols in the area,  including from the estuary  to inland areas.
He said the enhanced surveillance was aimed at detecting and preventing illegal activities, particularly the movement of undocumented migrants through the state's waters.

Title: Trump administration targets seven Minnesota judges over ICE raid comments
Article:
WASHINGTON: The US Justice Department asked a court Wednesday to punish federal judges in Minnesota who spoke to the media and criticised aggressive raids carried out in that state by Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
It was the latest twist in a clash between the Trump administration and federal judges who have at times thwarted his drive to deport millions of immigrants lacking residency papers.
On September 17, The New York Times published an article that quoted Judge Patrick Schiltz, the chief judge at Minnesota's federal district court during a series of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) raids last winter in Minneapolis, and six of the judge's colleagues on the bench.
Schiltz had already gained notoriety during the peak of those raids by saying publicly that ICE had probably violated more court orders in January 2026 than other federal agencies had in their entire decades of existence.
In an interview for the Times article, Schiltz said ICE's behaviour had sparked such chaos in his court that it "created a grave threat to the rule of law." He said he thought the violations of court orders stemmed mainly from incompetence and staffing shortages.
It is rare for a judge to speak out publicly like that, the Times said.
He and the other six judges quoted in the article declined to talk about ongoing cases, but they did agree to address the tumult of last winter during the ICE operation dubbed "Metro Surge" and the tension it triggered between Schiltz's court and the Justice Department, the paper said.
The Justice Department announced Wednesday it had filed a judicial misconduct complaint against Schiltz and the other six judges at a federal appeals court. It accuses them of ethics violations by speaking publicly about cases pending in court.
The department asked an appeals court to investigate these judges, Attorney General Todd Blanche told a press conference.
The department has "asked that these judges recuse themselves from every case involving DHS, either criminal or civil in nature, because of the obvious bias they have shown in this article with the New York Times," Blanche said. DHS stands for Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE.
During operation "Metro Surge" ICE agents shot and killed two American citizens taking part in street protests against the immigration raids, triggering national outrage and prompting the administration to wind down the operation.
The administration says the raids netted the arrest of 4,000 people who were in the country illegally.--AFP

Title: 'Excessive minimum wage increase could lead to cost shock for businesses' - ACCCIM
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:   The Associated Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry of Malaysia (Acccim) has cautioned that an excessive minimum wage adjustment could create a cost shock for businesses, particularly those operating on thin profit margins.
Its president, Datuk Ng Yih Pyng, said businesses had already been inundated with multiple cost increases over the past two years amid a challenging operating environment.
While not against an increase in the minimum wage, he cautioned that an overly large adjustment could  impact micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
Ng said the level should strike a balance between improving workers' incomes and ensuring the operational survival of MSMEs.
He noted that businesses with thin margins could pass higher labour costs on to consumers through higher retail prices, adding to inflationary pressures.
He said sectors with a large presence of low-wage and entry-level workers, including retail, restaurants, food services, agriculture and small and medium-sized manufacturing, would be particularly exposed to higher operating costs.
Ng also highlighted the "ripple effect" of a minimum wage increase, whereby workers earning slightly above the minimum threshold could also seek higher wages.
He said this could increase overall payroll costs as businesses adjusted wages across different levels to maintain existing wage differentials.
At the same time, higher minimum wages would directly increase employers' statutory contributions to the Employees Provident Fund, Social Security Organisation and Employment Insurance System.
Ng said a one-size-fits-all approach to minimum wage increases could put smaller businesses at risk of having to reduce their workforce or shut down.
Instead, wage increases should take into account productivity and performance, sector-specific financial capacity, as well as broader economic and business conditions, he said.
Acccim, he said, called on the government to consider a tiered regional  system rather than a uniform national rate, taking into account differences in the cost of living, labour market conditions and levels of economic development across states.
He said a single wage floor could place disproportionate pressure on businesses in economically weaker regions, while workers in high-cost areas might still struggle to meet basic living expenses.
Under a tiered approach, minimum wages could be calibrated to local conditions, allowing higher wages in high-cost cities while helping low-margin businesses in weaker markets manage labour costs and reduce the risk of job losses.
