Title: Ex-UiTM Holdings CEO charged with CBT over RM37.37m meant for Pahang solar project
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — A former group chief executive officer of UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd was charged today with criminal breach of trust involving RM37.37 million earmarked for a large-scale solar power project in Pahang.
Azlizan Fadzil, 53, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read to him before Sessions Court judge Datuk Mohd Nasir Nordin, the
New Straits Times
(NST) reported.
According to the charge, Azlizan was entrusted in his capacity as chief executive officer with RM37,374,612.68 intended for investment in a 50-megawatt large-scale solar photovoltaic power generation project in Gambang.
He is accused of dishonestly misappropriating the money by making payments for purposes other than the intended investment.
The alleged offence took place between February 2 and October 2, 2017, at Affin Bank Berhad’s UiTM Shah Alam branch at Menara Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah, according to the report.
Azlizan was charged under Section 409 of the Penal Code, which carries a jail term of between two and 20 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
He told the court interpreter that he understood the charge and the penalties.
NST reported that Azlizan arrived at the courtroom shortly before 9am in a wheelchair, accompanied by several family members.

Title: Supply chain resilience tops agenda as Singapore DPM Gan Kim Yong visits Malaysia
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 1 — Singapore Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong arrived in Malaysia today for a one-day working visit, with strengthening economic ties and supply chain resilience between the two countries at the top of the agenda.
The commercial aircraft carrying Gan and his delegation landed at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 here at 9.40am.
Gan, who is also Singapore trade and industry minister, was warmly welcomed by Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (Miti) Deputy Secretary-General (Investment and Management) R. Jaya Singam.
During the visit, Gan is scheduled to meet Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and attend a business luncheon with the Malaysia-Singapore Business Council in Kuala Lumpur.
He is also slated to co-chair the Third Annual Ministerial Dialogue (AMD) between MITI and Singapore’s Ministry of Trade and Industry and meet Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir in Putrajaya.
The Third AMD will focus on strengthening bilateral cooperation in investment, trade and the economy, particularly in supply chain resilience and the halal industry, amid an increasingly complex and uncertain global geo-economic and geopolitical environment.
A key outcome expected from the dialogue is the adoption of the Terms of Reference for the Malaysia-Singapore Supply Chain Working Group, aimed at enhancing supply chain resilience, coordinating crisis responses, facilitating the cross-border movement of goods, and minimising disruptions to both countries’ supply chains.
The visit also provides an opportunity for both countries to explore new areas of mutually beneficial cooperation, particularly in investment, trade and the halal industry.
In 2025, Singapore was Malaysia’s second-largest trading partner globally and largest among Asean member states, with bilateral trade valued at RM402.8 billion.
During the same period, Singapore was also Malaysia’s largest source of foreign direct investment among Asean member states, with investments totalling RM53.4 billion. — Bernama

Title: AI, intelligence-led probes and fair enforcement: MACC’s five priorities at 59
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — Nearly six decades into its fight against corruption, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) continues to strengthen its strategies to ensure enforcement, prevention and integrity remain at the heart of its work.
As the agency marks its 59th anniversary today, MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman outlined five leadership priorities to guide his administration: uncompromising integrity, fair and equitable enforcement, proactive prevention, adopting technology, and transparency and public trust.
According to Abd Halim, the dynamic nature of corruption offenses requires MACC to remain agile in transforming and adapting its investigative approaches to meet the challenges of a new era.
“Integrity is the cornerstone of the fight against corruption and cannot be compromised under any circumstances, whether when making decisions, conducting investigations or carrying out our daily responsibilities,” he said in an interview in conjunction with MACC’s 59th anniversary.
He said the second pillar is reflected in MACC’s approach to fair enforcement, including its decision to suspend the practice of requiring individuals under probe to wear orange lock-up attire during remand proceedings in court, aimed at countering negative perceptions of those who have yet to be charged.
“For MACC, firm enforcement does not mean disregarding the principles of justice. We can take a firm stand against corruption while at the same time respecting the rights, dignity and due process of every individual under investigation,” he said.
On the third pillar, Abd Halim stressed MACC’s priority of reinforcing proactive prevention by identifying systemic weaknesses and closing loopholes before corruption takes root, particularly through the Governance Investigation Division (BPT).
He said the BPT’s role, under Sections 7(c), (d) and (e) of the MACC Act 2009, includes reviewing the practices, systems and procedures of public bodies, as well as advising relevant parties on measures to mitigate corruption risks.
“At the same time, MACC has enhanced enforcement by moving beyond simply waiting for reports and adopting a more proactive approach through Intelligence-Based Investigation (IBI) to detect and uncover corruption. We want to act before problems escalate,” he said.
Addressing the fourth pillar, Abd Halim said MACC is focusing on technology, digitalisation, data analytics and artificial intelligence (AI) to boost operational efficiency and improve transparency in investigations.
He said the move reflects a shift to a more proactive enforcement approach, with MACC moving away from simply waiting for complaints and instead acting swiftly through IBI.
“Combining data analytics, AI and digital systems helps investigators process large volumes of information more quickly, including identifying anomalies, tracing financial flows and detecting links that may be difficult to uncover through conventional methods,” he said.
Meanwhile, he said MACC’s operations this year are focused on four high-impact sectors: government procurement, enforcement agencies, public funds or special allocations, and government revenue and income.
He said MACC received 5,239 reports and opened 842 investigation papers between January and Aug 31, leading to 803 arrests involving 428 private-sector individuals and 311 civil servants, adding that the cases included 352 for receiving bribes, 278 for submitting false claims and 78 for offering bribes.
“Between January and July 31, MACC also recorded a total of RM55,314,743 through forfeitures, compounds, settlements, asset freezes and seizures,” he said.
However, he stressed that statistics alone do not determine MACC’s success, saying its real impact lay in bringing offenders to justice, recovering funds lost through leakages and closing gaps in the system.
Referring to high-profile cases involving 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) and SRC International, Abd Halim said the investigations have expanded the agency’s expertise in financial forensics, cross-border investigations and asset recovery.
“As of last year, MACC had recovered RM31.3 billion, or 74.5 per cent, of the RM42 billion in 1MDB funds that were misappropriated,” he said.
He said other high-impact operations have also exposed various forms of corruption, including a ‘counter setting’ syndicate, Op Parasit, delays in padi fertiliser distribution in Kedah, the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Tabung Haji, and Retirement Fund Incorporated’s (KWAP) RM200 million investment in eFishery.
He said enforcement action must be followed by systemic reforms, stronger internal controls, improved procedures and greater accountability to ensure every case uncovered serves as a lesson for the country.
“MACC’s true success is not merely measured by its ability to uncover cases, but by whether the outcome helps narrow opportunities for corruption, strengthen systems and boost public confidence in the country’s institutions,” he said.
Established in January 2009 under the MACC Act 2009, MACC replaced the Anti-Corruption Agency (ACA) and serves as the country’s sole independent body leading anti-corruption prevention and enforcement efforts. — Bernama

Title: Three homes hit by mudslide after heavy rain in Sungai Petani
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 1 — Three houses in Kampung Serukam here were affected by a mudslide following heavy rain yesterday afternoon.
The incident is believed to have occurred after heavy rain began at about 12.30pm, causing a collapse at a nearby housing project site, before water and mud flowed into residents’ homes.
One of the victims, Siti Aishah Hassan, 44, said her parents-in-law’s house was inundated with water to a depth of about 0.5 metres, but both had been moved to a safe location before the incident as they had suffered strokes.
“I cannot imagine what would have happened if my parents-in-law had been in the house. The heavy rain caused the water to flow strongly and rapidly, and it rose within a very short time.
“Household furnishings and electrical appliances, including the refrigerator and washing machine, were overturned, while other belongings were scattered. The inside of the house was also covered in mud,” she told reporters here.
She said her brother-in-law, Rashid Khamis, 44, who was asleep in the lower part of the house, also managed to save himself after realising that water and mud had entered the house.
Meanwhile, Scientex SP Astana project site supervisor Mohd Haniff Ramli said three houses were affected in the incident, including two located within the project site.
“About a year ago, a similar incident also occurred. We sent a team to clean the affected houses and also cleared the road.
“For now, the residents’ houses are being cleaned. After this, we will assess the damage for further action,” he said.
It is understood that the affected residents living within the project site had been informed of a proposal to relocate them to another location, but the matter is still being negotiated between both parties.
The housing project is currently in the earthworks and construction phase. — Bernama

Title: SpaceX donates 50 Starlink kits to Malaysia for disaster preparedness
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — United States Aerospace Company, SpaceX, yesterday donated 50 units of Starlink kits to Malaysia to support the country’s disaster preparedness, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar said the contribution was presented by a SpaceX delegation that made a courtesy call on him at the Perdana Putra Building in Putrajaya, which was also attended by Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
Anwar said the meeting, among other things, discussed efforts to strengthen strategic cooperation through Starlink, the satellite internet service operated by the company, with a specific focus on expanding network access to residents in rural areas.
“I appreciate Starlink’s role in supporting the government’s efforts to expand coverage and improve the quality of internet access through the National Digital Network (Jendela), including in rural areas of Sabah and Sarawak as well as Orang Asli settlements in the Peninsula.”
“I also welcome the operation of Starlink’s Point of Presence (PoP) infrastructure in Cyberjaya to smoothen local data traffic and improve service quality for users,” he said in a Facebook post.
At the same time, Anwar stressed that technological advancement must bring tangible benefits to the people, alongside ensuring that cybersecurity, data protection, and safe internet usage continue to be given priority in tandem with the expansion of internet access.
“We want to ensure that communities in rural areas also enjoy quality and safe internet access so that they are not left behind in the country’s current of progress,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Guardiola pledges loyalty to Man City as punishment looms over financial rule breach scandal
Article:
MANCHESTER, Oct 1 — Former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola threw his weight behind the club on Wednesday after a bombshell verdict on Premier League financial rule breaches plunged their future into serious doubt.
The former boss broke his silence 24 hours after it was announced that the Abu Dhabi-backed club had been found guilty of more than 100 breaches of financial rules in the world’s richest domestic league.
Premier League chief executive Richard Masters described the disciplinary case and the decision by an independent commission as the “most significant in Premier League history”.
He said City “systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade”, adding that the league was committed to a swift resolution.
The likely punishment is uncertain but, according to Premier League rules, City could face a substantial points deduction, a fine or even expulsion from the top division.
The 10-time English champions, who continue to deny any wrongdoing, have vowed to appeal and have until Friday to do so.
Guardiola, who was a vocal supporter of the club over the issue before leaving the Etihad in May, broke his silence in a post on X.
“I want every single @ManCity fan to know I am here, more than ever,” said the Spaniard, who won six Premier League titles and the Champions League in a golden decade at the helm.
“I am, always have been, always will be, behind my club, my owner, my chairman, (CEO) Ferran (Soriano), the players, staff, (manager) Enzo (Maresca) and you, our unique supporters.
“Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all.”
‘Significant breach’
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he did not want to see the club’s Emirati owners walk away as a result of the case.
“I would be really concerned to lose them,” he told the BBC, highlighting the investment the Abu Dhabi United Group had made in Manchester, where Burnham was mayor until June.
But English football’s independent regulator, David Kogan, said that his body has the power to assess the suitability of club owners and executives “where appropriate”, when there is “clear evidence of wrongdoing by individuals”.
The Premier League, which first charged City in 2023, announced the findings of the commission on Tuesday.
The commission found City arranged “sham” deals to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs by more than £900 million (RM4.9 billion) between 2009 and 2018, a period in which they won three Premier League titles and other silverware.
In doing so, they concealed the true state of their finances but the commission said that the club were “significantly in breach of both the Premier League’s and Uefa’s spending limits”.
The commission found the club guilty on all charges related to breaches of financial rules over the nine-year period.
They have also been found guilty of most of the charges they faced in relation to a failure to cooperate with a Premier League investigation.
Sky Sports
reported that City’s stadium and shirt sponsor Etihad has categorically denied any implication the Emirati airline has been involved in improper commercial arrangements and threatened to take legal action against the Premier League.
Punishment
Everton and Nottingham Forest were given points deductions in the 2023/24 season for single breaches of financial sustainability rules.
On that basis, City could face relegation given the sheer weight of the case against them.
There is speculation they could even be stripped of their titles.
“If the appeal fails, Manchester City cannot stay in the league, they have to suffer. And I say that as a supporter and a fan,” said the club’s former chairman, David Bernstein.
Former City defender Micah Richards, who was part of the side that won the club’s first top-flight league title for 44 years in 2012, said the uncertainty was “heartbreaking”.
“I achieved my dream at Manchester City, but then to hear these reports, and not only me as an ex-player, but the fans, what they have to go through, absolutely devastating,” Richards said on The Rest is Football podcast.
City have become the Premier League’s dominant force since the 2008 takeover by Sheikh Mansour, the vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates.
The team are next in action against Liverpool at Anfield on October 11, where they will take on the club who have been their closest challengers over the past decade. — AFP

Title: RM6,000 work permit deal leads to arrest of alleged fake Immigration officer
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 1 — The Melaka Immigration Department (JIM) has arrested a housewife suspected of impersonating a senior immigration officer and offering services to process work pass applications for foreigners.
Melaka Immigration director Anirwan Fauzee Mohd Aini said the woman, in her 50s, was detained in a raid under Op Serkap at a cafe in Taman Malim Jaya here at about 6 pm yesterday.
Anirwan Fauzee said following the arrest, another raid was conducted at a condominium in Kota Laksamana, where various items believed to belong to the suspect were seized to assist in further investigations.
The items seized included a set of black uniform with accessories, a pair of senior immigration officer rank insignia, a pair of JIM collar badges, a JIM integrity badge, two grey headscarves, two black T-shirts bearing the JIM logo and a forged JIM identification card.
“When she was detained at the cafe, the suspect was dealing with a Chinese national who claimed to have paid about RM6,000 to obtain a work permit. So far, about three victims, including two Malaysians, are believed to have been duped by the suspect.
“The suspect offered services to apply for work passes for foreigners requiring work permits or temporary visit passes for employment, without the employer or foreigner concerned having to go to an Immigration office,” he said at a press conference here yesterday.
He said preliminary investigations found that the suspect had been carrying out the impersonation and fraud activities for between one and two years, operating alone and approaching employers or foreigners who appeared desperate to obtain work permits.
He said the mother of five had also uploaded pictures of herself fully dressed in the department’s uniform on social media to convince employers that she was an officer of the department.
Anirwan Fauzee said the suspect was remanded for four days from yesterday until Saturday to assist investigations under Sections 56(1)(k) and 56(1)(l) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.
“JIM Melaka has also issued witness summonses to the victims or clients of the suspect as well as her husband to assist in further investigations.
“In this regard, the public is advised to remain vigilant and not be easily deceived by individuals offering unofficial immigration services, but instead deal directly with the nearest JIM office,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Zulkifli: Tabung Haji RCI follow-up must be firm and comprehensive
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Zulkifli Hasan is focusing on ensuring firm and comprehensive follow-up actions are taken on the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji (TH) after appearing before the Parliamentary Public Accounts Committee (PAC).
He said the move was crucial to protect the trust of millions of depositors and safeguard the sanctity of Islamic assets.
“The main focus at this juncture is to ensure that follow-up actions on the TH RCI Report are completed in a firm and comprehensive manner,” he said in a Facebook post.
Zulkifli said he had reviewed all relevant documents, including the Tabung Haji Act and the RCI Report, before attending the more than two-hour session.
He described his first appearance before PAC as similar to a PhD viva voce — an oral examination where researchers defend their dissertations before an assessment panel, as various questions were raised by committee members.
“Thankfully, this preparation enabled me to answer the questions raised calmly and confidently, with Allah’s will and permission,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Zulkifli condemns Al-Aqsa incursions, backs call for international action
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — The incursion by illegal Israeli settlers into the Al-Aqsa Mosque Complex and the Ibrahimi Mosque in Palestine constitutes a clear violation of international law, asserted the Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Senator Zulkifli Hasan.
In this regard, he said he strongly condemns the series of extreme provocations carried out under the tight control of Israeli security forces.
He noted that the Al-Aqsa Mosque as the first ‘Qibla’ (direction of prayer) for Muslims represents a red line that must be defended by the entire Muslim community without compromise.
“The Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) fully supports the firm stance taken by Wisma Putra and calls upon the international community to take appropriate action in response to the Zionist regime’s insolence and to demand accountability,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.
Zulkifli reiterated his unwavering solidarity with the Palestinian people’s struggle to defend their rights and sovereignty, with Jerusalem as their capital.
At the same time, he urged Muslims across the country to remain united, increase their prayers, and voice their objections to uphold the sanctity of Al-Aqsa Mosque and ensure the safety of the Palestinian people. — Bernama

Title: Tourist dies after losing consciousness during Tioman scuba dive
Article:
KUANTAN, Oct 1 — A 55-year-old Afghan man died while taking part in a Discovery Scuba Diving (DSD) activity in the waters off Kampung Salang, Pulau Tioman, Rompin, yesterday.
Rompin police chief Supt Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi said the victim, Mohammed Seyar Musazay, who was residing in California, United States, was confirmed dead at about 12.40pm after being taken to the Kampung Tekek Health Clinic.
He said initial investigations found that the victim was on holiday in Pulau Tioman with his 24-year-old daughter from Kuala Lumpur and had been staying at a chalet in Kampung Salang since September 26.
“At about 11am, the victim, his daughter and a scuba instructor went out to take part in the DSD activity.
“Before starting the activity, the victim and his daughter were briefed on the use of diving equipment. They were then taken to the beach for practical training and subsequently to the sea,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Sharif Shai said the dive lasted about 20 minutes at a depth of six metres, with the victim initially appearing to be in good condition and showing no problems.
“When the activity was about to end, the instructor helped the victim’s daughter return to the surface first from a depth of about three metres before he noticed the victim struggling to reach the surface about three metres away from him.
“The instructor then approached the victim and found that his breathing apparatus (regulator) had become detached from his mouth and that he was unconscious,” he said.
Sharif Shai said the victim was then taken to the beach before being transported by a villager’s boat to the Kampung Tekek Health Clinic, where he was pronounced dead.
“The victim’s body was taken to Teluk Gading by a Marine Police boat at about 4.50pm before being sent to the Tengku Ampuan Afzan Hospital (HTAA) in Kuantan for a post-mortem,” he added. — Bernama

Title: At Dr Hasmah’s grave, Malaysians reflect on a life that touched generations
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — Three days after the demise of Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali, her resting place at Pusara Negara continues to see a steady stream of visitors, offering prayers and expressions of gratitude.
While some knew the late Tun personally and others knew her only through stories and her contributions to the nation, the sentiment shared by those visiting the grave remained the same: people from diverse backgrounds and generations paid their respects to a figure who had become an integral part of the country’s history.
A Bernama survey found that visitors, including those from the surrounding areas of Putrajaya and Cyberjaya, began arriving as early as noon to spend time in quiet reflection and offer prayers for the late Tun.
Muslim visitors took the opportunity to recite the Surah Yasin and pray by the graveside, while visitors of various ethnicities also came to pay their last respects.
The atmosphere at the gravesite was emotional, with some visitors unable to hold back their tears while praying, and others wept during interviews with Bernama, despite never having met the deceased in person.
For several medical officers from the National Centre of Excellence for Mental Health, the visit held special significance, as they had grown up during the era of Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and Tun Dr Siti Hasmah.
Among them, Dr Chandravany A/P Supramaniam, 50, said the discipline, punctuality, and family values instilled in her life were influenced by the couple, whom she regards as role models for her own family.
“I was born and raised during the era of Tun (Dr) M and (Tun Dr) Siti Hasmah. The upbringing I received from my father also reflected the values of that era... discipline, punctuality — everything came from both of them. Regarding family unity, they served as role models for me and my family,” she said.
Also taking the opportunity amidst a busy schedule was Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) chief executive officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin. She noted that memories of the late Tun remain vivid among the journalists who covered her activities since the early days of their careers.
Nur-ul Afida, who began covering the late Tun’s activities between 1984 and 1986, said that Tun Dr Siti Hasmah always treated journalists and photographers warmly, including during events at the prime minister’s official residence.
She said the late Tun never allowed her position as the prime minister’s wife to create a barrier when interacting with guests or media personnel.
“The treatment extended to us — journalists and photographers — at that time was incredibly warm. We were invited to eat and drink, just like the other distinguished guests.
“From that, we could see another side of her; she did not stand on ceremony regarding her status as the prime minister’s wife, but instead treated everyone present at the official residence as her personal guests,” she said.
According to her, two issues the late Tun frequently emphasised during media interviews were children’s education and women’s welfare.
She noted that her words and views on the importance of education and women’s efforts to advance themselves served as a source of inspiration for many, including herself.
“Even simple words or expressions can serve as a great source of inspiration for many,” she said.
Meanwhile, a teacher, Wan Mohd Khairi Wan Hassan from Sekolah Kebangsaan took the opportunity to bring a group of students to visit the Siti Hasmah’s grave, even though the visit was not part of their original itinerary for the trip to Putrajaya.
He said the group comprising 40 students and seven teachers had originally scheduled a tour of Putrajaya but seized the opportunity to visit the grave after a request was made.
A Bernama survey also indicated that the number of visitors is expected to rise towards the end of the week, as members of the public continue to take the opportunity to pay their respects to Siti Hasmah.
Tun Dr Siti Hasmah, 100, passed away at the National Heart Institute (IJN) on the morning of September 28 and following a state funeral was laid to rest at the Pusara Negara in Precinct 20, Putrajaya, on the same day. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia restores parliamentary service after 34 years as new law takes effect
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — The Parliamentary Services Act 2025 (Act 869) and related amendments to the Federal Constitution take effect today.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the Act’s enactment is a significant achievement for the Madani Government’s institutional reform agenda and a historic milestone for the Malaysian Parliament, 34 years after the Parliamentary Services Act 1963 (Act 394) was repealed under the Constitution (Amendment) Act 1992 (Act A837), effective Nov 20, 1992.
“More than three decades on, Act 869 restores Parliament’s autonomy by creating a dedicated parliamentary service, giving it greater independence and efficiency in managing its administration, human resources and affairs.
“This will further strengthen Parliament’s position as the highest legislative body in the country’s parliamentary democracy,” she said in a statement today.
She said the Madani Government also expressed its gratitude to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, for granting consent to set Oct 1, 2026, as the date on which Act 869 and related amendments to the Federal Constitution would come into force.
The reform also reflects the Madani Government’s commitment to upholding the doctrine of separation of powers and the system of checks and balances among the legislative, executive and judicial branches.
“With stronger institutional autonomy, Parliament can carry out its constitutional functions and responsibilities to the people more independently, effectively and credibly,” Azalina said.
She also thanked Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also Leader of the House, the Cabinet and all stakeholders, including non-governmental and civil society organisations, for their cooperation in bringing about the reform.
“The Madani Government will continue to pursue its institutional reform agenda in a structured and sustained manner to strengthen the country’s democratic institutions and ensure public confidence in national institutions is maintained,” she said.
The Parliamentary Services Bill 2025 was tabled for its first reading in the Dewan Rakyat on Feb 24, 2025, followed by its second reading on March 4, 2025.
The Dewan Rakyat passed the Bill on March 5, followed by the Dewan Negara on March 20, 2025. Sultan Ibrahim consented on July 9, and the Bill was gazetted on July 18, 2025. — Bernama

Title: MACC urges tighter governance at Felda and subsidiaries over two projects
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has proposed governance improvements to the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) and two of its subsidiaries to strengthen the management of two projects under the agency.
In a statement yesterday, MACC said the subsidiaries involved were FIC Supplies Sdn Bhd (FIC Supplies) and FIC Integrated Property Management (FIC IPM).
The recommendations were put forward by MACC’s Governance Investigation Division (BPT) to enhance governance in the implementation of the Agro Park (Commercial) Project and the Cattle Trading Pilot Project.
Among the recommendations for Felda was the restructuring of FIC IPM’s role as an independent advisory panel to ensure that all views and advice provided are objective, transparent and free from conflicts of interest.
“MACC BPT also recommended that Felda strengthen its procurement and transaction management procedures by establishing specific Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for procurement methods involving request for proposal (RFP) and variation orders,” the statement said.
MACC said the measures were important to ensure that the processes were carried out consistently, systematically and transparently in line with established regulations and internal controls.
The recommendations also include improving existing procedures related to FIC Supplies’ sales and purchase activities to strengthen controls and governance in the company’s transactions.
The proposals were presented by MACC BPT deputy director I Maznah Che Muda at Menara Felda here on Monday.
Meanwhile, Felda and its subsidiaries welcomed the recommendations to strengthen governance, transparency and integrity within the agency, while expressing their commitment to implement them in stages.
The agreement to adopt the recommendations was formalised through the Governance Improvement Report signed by Felda deputy director-general (Corporate Services) Muhammad Fitri Othman, FIC Group chief executive officer Syed Fadil Syed Sofi and MACC BPT director Datuk Mohd Zaki Hassan. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027 to consider cost pressures on small businesses, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — The government will study the cost pressures in procurement and operations faced by small enterprises following the global supply crisis when formulating Budget 2027, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the matter was among those raised during the Budget 2027 engagement session with representatives of associations and Bumiputera contractor companies held at Perdana Putra, Putrajaya, yesterday.
He said all views and suggestions put forward during the session have been taken into account to be properly examined in the preparation of the budget.
“The Madani Government will ensure that Budget 2027 can open up wider avenues and opportunities so that the people and businesses can build their capabilities and uphold the dignity of the nation’s people,” he said in a Facebook post.
According to the calendar for the Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament, which begins on October 5, the tabling of Budget 2027 is scheduled for October 9. — Bernama

Title: F1 weekend drives 160pc surge in accommodation searches for KL and Sepang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Malaysia is seeing a surge in travel interest ahead of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit, with accommodation searches for Kuala Lumpur, Sepang and surrounding areas jumping more than 160 per cent year-on-year for the October 2 to 4 race weekend.
Airbnb country head for India and South-east Asia Amanpreet Bajaj said the surge highlights how major sporting events continue to serve as key drivers of tourism and economic activity.
“Travel today is increasingly shaped by experiences. People are making plans around concerts, festivals, sporting events and other occasions that bring communities together, and these experiences can create new opportunities for destinations to welcome visitors.
“From Kuala Lumpur’s vibrant city experiences to local attractions, Airbnb gives travellers the flexibility to plan a stay around the experiences, whether that means making a weekend of it or exploring more of the destination beyond the events,” he said in a statement yesterday.
According to data released by the platform, the sharp increase was driven mainly by international travellers from Singapore, China, Indonesia, Australia, the United Kingdom and the United States, who accounted for approximately 75 per cent of total searches.
Within the surrounding areas, Kuala Lumpur accounted for more than 60 per cent of searches, followed by Sepang at nearly 25 per cent, alongside Petaling and Hulu Langat.
The statement noted that while travellers are looking towards Sepang and neighbouring areas for accommodation closer to the circuit and the airport, Kuala Lumpur remains the primary base for visitors.
The data also revealed that about 80 per cent of searches extended beyond the race weekend, with the median intended length of stay reaching nearly six nights.
Trips involving two guests accounted for more than one-third of searches, while bookings involving two or more guests made up close to seven in 10. — Bernama

Title: Meeting with 25 Negeri Sembilan assemblymen did not discuss MB’s royal audience, says Jalaluddin
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — A special meeting with 25 Negeri Sembilan state assemblymen last night did not discuss Tuesday’s audience between Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim and Negeri Sembilan Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, said state Umno chief Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias.
He said the discussion focused more on efforts to ensure that all elected representatives from the government bloc remained committed to carrying out their responsibilities in their constituencies, as well as strengthening the party.
He said Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had urged the assemblymen not to be affected by current developments and to continue prioritising service to the people following the political situation in the state.
“We conveyed a narrative and a guideline for the 25 assemblymen to carry out their duties in their constituencies, strengthen the party and also fulfil their responsibilities as elected representatives,” he told reporters after the meeting at Menara Dato Onn here.
He said the meeting was also attended by Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki and BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Zambry Abdul Kadir. — Bernama

Title: Meta given until Oct 2 to respond over WhatsApp account issues, says MCMC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is demanding a comprehensive explanation from Meta regarding issues involving WhatsApp accounts that have been suspended, rendered inaccessible, or accessed without authorisation.
In a statement yesterday, MCMC informed that a total of 92 complaints related to the issue have been received by the commission so far.
According to the commission, an official request was submitted to Meta on September 25, followed by discussions with the technology company on September 28.
“Meta has requested until October 2 to provide feedback regarding the matter. MCMC urges Meta to provide a comprehensive explanation as well as an immediate solution for the affected user accounts, and will determine subsequent actions based on that feedback,” the statement read.
Earlier yesterday, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said he had instructed MCMC to issue a statement clarifying Meta’s response regarding the issues of hacking and the deactivation of WhatsApp accounts.
He added that he has yet to receive updates on the outcome of the discussions between MCMC and Meta concerning the matter.
Earlier, MCMC announced that it was examining the complaints received and had forwarded the relevant cases to Meta for clarification and further action and the commission also explained that account takeovers or hacking, and account blocking, are two different matters.
According to MCMC, accounts hacked by irresponsible parties risk being misused for scam activities, spam, or violations of WhatsApp’s terms of service, which can ultimately lead to the accounts being blocked by the platform. — Bernama

Title: ECRL explained: How fast, how far and when will Malaysia’s new East Coast rail link open?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — The East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) could begin carrying passengers as early as mid-December, ahead of its original January 2027 launch target.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said on September 23 that the government wants to see the ECRL completed before committing to other high-speed rail projects in the country.
Stretching 665km, the electrified rail network is set to transform travel between the East Coast and the Klang Valley, linking Kota Bharu in Kelantan to Port Klang in Selangor via Terengganu, Pahang and the Greater Klang Valley.
Here’s what we know so far about the ECRL and how close it is to opening:
1. How fast is the ECRL, and where will it run?
The ECRL network is being developed in two phases: the Kota Bharu-to-Gombak stretch, originally slated to begin operations in January 2027, and the Gombak-to-Port Klang section, scheduled to open in January 2028.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said in August that the first phase was on track for completion in December, with the government pushing for passenger operations to begin as early as the middle of that month.
The passenger fleet will comprise 11 six-car Electric Multiple Unit (EMU) train sets built by China Railway Rolling Stock Corporation (CRRC) Dalian.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke challenged MRL and CCCC in August 2026 to bring forward the start of ECRL operations to mid-December. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) chief executive officer Datuk Seri Darwis Abdul Razak told Bernama in September that the ECRL would nearly halve the travel time between Kota Bharu and Gombak, from about seven hours by road to around four hours.
ECRL services could also run from Gombak to Kuala Terengganu in about three hours and from Gombak to Kuantan in just one hour and 35 minutes on an express service, according to Loke.
The full ECRL network is planned to have 20 stations, comprising 10 passenger-only stations and 10 stations serving both passengers and freight.
2. How many passengers can the ECRL carry?
Each six-car EMU can carry up to 425 passengers in an all-economy configuration.
The passenger trains will operate at speeds of up to 160km/h and are equipped with facilities including toilets, luggage racks, food-and-beverage counters, prayer rooms with ablution areas and facilities for passengers with disabilities.
Loke has said the network could eventually carry up to 10,000 passengers a day, depending on service frequency.
3. Why is the ECRL being pushed for an earlier opening?
Loke recently challenged MRL and China Communications Construction Company (CCCC) to get the first phase of the ECRL running in time for the year-end school holidays in mid-December.
The earlier launch, however, remains subject to testing and commissioning being completed satisfactorily and without compromising safety requirements.
CCCC is the ECRL’s engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning contractor, while operations and maintenance will be handled through a joint venture involving MRL and China Communications Construction Company ECRL Sdn Bhd (CCCECRL).
A general view of the ECRL tunnel in Section 2A in Rawang during a technical site visit on October 31, 2025. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
4. How close is the ECRL to opening?
MRL is already deploying comprehensive inspection trains (CITs) to detect potential problems along the rail network ahead of the planned start of operations.
More than 40 CIT test runs and 12 freight train tests had been carried out as of September 18, CCCECRL project director and senior adviser Kong Qi told
The Edge Malaysia
recently.
The testing has included speeds of up to 176km/h, above the ECRL’s planned passenger operating speed of 160km/h.
The trains are expected to complete full runs between Kota Bharu and Gombak by the end of September, before the mandatory Fault-Free Run (FFR) begins in October.
The Transport Ministry is also expected to announce ECRL fares by the end of the year.
5. Will the ECRL carry freight too?
Yes. The ECRL will also deploy electric locomotives for freight services along the network.
The freight trains can operate at speeds of up to 80km/h and haul as many as 45 wagons, with a maximum freight capacity of 3,500 tonnes per trip, the
New Straits Times
reported last December.
The electric locomotives are also equipped with intelligent human-machine interfaces and millisecond-level safety monitoring systems covering braking, fire protection and high-voltage insulation.

Title: In Johor Bahru, firemen rescue 44 pupils and teachers in kindergarten trapped by flash flood
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 30 – Firemen managed to rescue 37 pupils and seven teachers who were earlier trapped in the Umiku Sayang Kindergarten and Nursery on Jalan Muhd Amin here after it was inundated by a flash floods today.
Larkin Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Senior Fire Officer I Nakish Nekmat said that authorities received an distress call regarding the incident at 3.53pm.
Following the call, a team of 10 firemen – equipped with a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT) and an Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) unit – were dispatched to the scene that was located about 10 kilometres away.
“The firemen arrived at 4.14pm and immediately conducted a rescue operation using a volunteer's boat to evacuate the trapped victims to the nearby Tepian Food Court Surau.
“All victims were successfully evacuated, and no injuries were reported," he said in a statement.
Continuous heavy rain this afternoon had caused flash flooding in several areas around the city.
Many were trapped in traffic after flood waters rose causing roads to be inaccessible to motorists.

Title: Ex-EPF CEO proposes employers pay higher EPF contributions for low-wage workers while reducing contributions for high-income staff
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — To help lower-salary workers save up more money for their retirement through the Employees Provident Fund (EPF), their employers could help put in more money towards their EPF savings, former EPF CEO Tan Sri Shahril Ridza Ridzuan said today.
Shahril, currently Axiata Group Berhad’s chairman, noted that Malaysia currently has one of the highest contribution rates from employees and their employers for retirement savings in EPF.
Currently in Malaysia, the law requires Malaysian employees below age 60 to contribute 11 per cent of their salary into their EPF retirement savings, while employers will have to contribute 13 per cent of the salary (if the employee’s salary is below RM5,000) or 12 per cent (if above RM5,000).
“So the contribution rate itself is not the problem. The problem has always been for the last 50, 60 years, the fact really that wages have not grown fast enough in Malaysia. So when your base is small, no matter how big your contribution rate, you are just not building your retirement savings fast enough,” he said as a speaker at EPF’s International Social Wellbeing Conference 2026 here titled “The Long Horizon”.
He commended the current federal government for its efforts on working towards having a progressive wage policy to make sure workers get a fair share of the economy: “And we need to continue that. We need to have much better progressive policies to make sure that the minimum wage keeps going up.”
Later, Shahril suggested that a progressive wage policy would not just cover workers’ income levels, and proposed that it be used to set policies on EPF contribution rates from employers.
“And I would actually propose and suggest basically that employers pay a much higher contribution rate for workers below a certain threshold, and compensated really by then having a much lower contribution rate for workers past the threshold.
“So for instance, if you are earning below RM5,000, why shouldn’t employers contribute say 15 per cent or 16 per cent to your EPF?
“That helps basically in terms of building your retirement savings. It’s progressive in the sense of basically allowing for lower-income workers to build their savings faster,” he said.
“But you can then compensate by saying, for instance, that any worker above, for instance RM10,000, employers should only contribute four per cent,” he said when giving a hypothetical example to illustrate his point.
He said this would also help to cap the amount of money that EPF manages for high-income workers, such as those who are already earning RM10,000 and if they are well on their way to achieving their financial retirement plans.
He said this would be a better method than the hypothetical method of giving different investment yields for those with lower and higher total EPF savings.
“So instead of basically differentiating between account yields for those with higher balances in EPF and lower balances, actually what you should do is to start capping this contributions of high-income earners to reduce the size of their balance sheet,” he said in giving his proposed solution.
Shahril was responding to a question on how lower-income workers and informal workers can also achieve a dignified retirement through their retirement savings.
Currently in Malaysia, the law requires Malaysian employees below age 60 to contribute 11 per cent of their salary into their EPF retirement savings, while employers will have to contribute 13 per cent of the salary (if the employee’s salary is below RM5,000) or 12 per cent (if above RM5,000). — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
Earlier during his session, Shahril said he believed that having differentiated yields for EPF accounts will never be the right solution, as the EPF base is too big in terms of the number of EPF contributors it has.
He also said introducing differentiated yields on EPF accounts would carry a “very high risk” of outflow of funds from top EPF account holders.
He said this hypothetical scenario leading to funds outflow would be bad for all EPF members, as part of the reason for EPF’s success is that a bigger Assets Under Management (AUM) or total assets managed would translate to lower cost for all.
Shahril said the actual debate should be about improving wealth inequality in Malaysia and a better transfer of wealth between capital owners and workers: “So the fight is not really about between whether you are high-wage earner or whether you are low-wage earner. It’s really between, are you an owner of capital and business, and whether you are essentially paying a fair share to the state in order to support these policies.”
Gig workers
As for gig workers, Shahril said they face an “invisible tax” as gig platforms do not contribute to EPF savings towards those working on their platforms, which means the platforms have a lower operating cost and can then outcompete traditional brick-and-mortar businesses and Mom-and-Pop stores.
He proposed that a revenue tax be imposed on gig platforms, and that the money raised from this tax could then be used to provide for EPF contributions for gig workers.
“So I think there are ways of doing it right? It’s just a matter of being creative around understanding the maths and understanding how to push those boundaries for the betterment of those workers and those gig workers who are probably under-covered at this point in time,” he said.

Title: EPF CEO outlines four priorities for Malaysia as Malaysians live longer, says all have role to play
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Malaysia now faces four priorities as Malaysians are expected to live longer lives, including shifting from just thinking about having money for retirement to having income for the remaining years, the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) CEO said today.
EPF CEO Ahmad Zulqarnain Onn noted that longevity is one of the biggest defining forces that will impact Malaysia, including its society and economy.
Based on experts who spoke at EPF’s International Social Wellbeing Conference 2026 (ISWC), Zulqarnain noted that the longevity policy or policy for longer lives would cover many areas such as labour markets, healthcare systems, digital systems, infrastructure and communities.
“Income security, health, care, work, and community all shape how well people live longer lives,” the retirement savings fund’s CEO said in his closing remarks at the two-day ISWC 2026 here.
He also said the responsibility for this must be shared by all, including individuals, families, employers, communities and the government.
He noted that speakers have spoken about the need for the government to play a stronger role especially for long-term care and basic income security.
“Individuals also have a part to play by preparing early, saving consistently, and making informed choices along the way. And employers have a role too, through the wages that they pay, the flexibility that they provide, and the opportunities they create for all the workers to stay economically active,” he said.
Noting that those at the conference have spoken about the need for Malaysia’s pension system to evolve, Zulqarnain said: “And as people live longer and patterns of work change, reform will be necessary to strengthen coverage, adequacy, equity and the sustainability of retirement income over a longer life.”
He then concluded by listing four priorities for Malaysia, including moving away from EPF members’ preference for lump sum withdrawal of retirement savings to a system of ensuring income to last one’s entire life.
“So one of the challenges that we face as a system is how do we move from saving for retirement, to securing income for life? We must help members convert a lifetime of savings into a reliable income stream that lasts as long as they do,” he said.
Currently, EPF members already have the option to withdraw their EPF savings via monthly payments under the i-Emas scheme, instead of withdrawing all their savings in one lump sum.
The monthly withdrawal method helps EPF members’ retirement savings last longer, as their remaining savings can continue to grow and provide them with dividends every year.
During the two-day conference, speakers spoke about about proposed methods and examples abroad that would enable people to continue to have income after retirement beyond what they have saved up, including through monthly payments via annuity insurances or variable annuities.
Secondly, Zulqarnain said there is a need to close the coverage gap, as currently only 60 per cent of Malaysia’s workforce have savings in the EPF.
“Many people who do hard work every single day in the informal sector - gig workers, older workers, and women whose caregiving responsibilities shorten their working years are too often excluded and remain without adequate protection.
“So, closing these gaps is going to require coordinated action,” he said.
Thirdly, there is a need to stand with EPF members throughout the course of their entire life and not just on retirement day, which means engaging with them even before retirement.
“This means engaging earlier and more consistently, working with partners across health, housing, elderly care, and also introducing change gradually and transparently so that public trust remains strong,” he said.
“And fourth and finally, we must continue to advocate for labour market reforms that result in better wages for the workers of Malaysia,” he said.
Noting that a lot of work remains, Zulqarnain said EPF cannot work alone on these issues and that it will take a community of leaders to work together to ensure progress on these topics.
The ISWC, which is themed “The Long Horizon” this year and in its 13th edition, had seen international and local experts speak on wide-ranging issues covering retirement savings and financial security, healthcare and long-term care, active and purposeful ageing, age-inclusive communities, intergenerational support and policy reforms.

Title: Selangor allocates RM100,000 to help wives and children wronged in maintenance issues
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 30 — The Selangor state government has allocated RM100,000 for the implementation of the Selangor Rahmah Maintainence Assistance Programme 2026 to strengthen social protection and welfare for women and children who have been wronged due to syariah judgement debtors.
Selangor Women’s Development and Community Welfare Committee chairman Anfaal Saari said that the temporary financial assistance is estimated to benefit up to 50 affected families while the law enforcement process is carried out.
He said the one-off assistance was distributed according to the rates set by the Family Support Division (BSK) of the Selangor Syariah Judiciary Department (JAKESS) at RM2,000 for the wife and RM1,000 for each child.
“This initiative is implemented through JAKESS to assist women and children who have a maintenance order from the Syariah Court but fail to receive payment from the judgement debtor.
“The state government wishes to emphasise that the main narrative of the Rahmah Maintainence Assistance is to provide temporary relief to women and children who have been wronged, and not as a substitute for the obligation of those who are supposed to provide alimony,” he said in a statement today.
Anfaal said the eligibility requirements and criteria are that the applicant must be a Muslim and reside in Selangor, with a household income below RM5,000 per month, and have a Syariah Court maintenance order that is still in effect but has been neglected or failed to be paid by the debtor.
In addition, applicants must meet the requirements and criteria set out in the Guidelines for the Disbursement of Advances and Alimony Assistance under the Family Support Division (BSK), Department of Syariah Judiciary Malaysia (JKSM).
He said any individual who meets the eligibility criteria can submit an application by directly visiting the JAKESS office through BSK to check their eligibility and submit the application form.
“The state government remains vigilant in ensuring the protection of women’s and children’s welfare rights continues to be upheld and not neglected in this state.
“In this regard, the state government urges all ex-husbands and fathers not to let go and to fully take responsibility in fulfilling the maintenance ordered by the Syariah Court for the sake of the children’s livelihood and future,” he also said. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi asks MCMC to clarify Meta’s response on WhatsApp issues
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 30 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has asked the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) to issue a statement clarifying Meta’s response to issues involving hacked and deactivated WhatsApp accounts.
However, he said he had yet to receive an update on discussions between MCMC and Meta on the matter.
“I have not had the opportunity to get an update on the outcome of the discussions. Meta had requested until 3 pm last Monday to submit its response to issues raised by MCMC concerning hacked and deactivated WhatsApp accounts.
“I will ask MCMC to issue a statement based on Meta’s response,” he told a press conference after the Cabinet meeting here today.
The media previously reported that MCMC had taken note of public concerns over WhatsApp accounts reportedly being hacked, blocked or rendered inaccessible.
The commission said it was reviewing the complaints received and had referred the cases to Meta for clarification and further action.
MCMC also stressed that account takeovers or hacking and account blocking were two separate issues.
It said hacked accounts could be misused by irresponsible parties for scams, spam or violations of WhatsApp’s terms of service, potentially resulting in the accounts being blocked by the platform.
On another development, Fahmi said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had instructed Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar to engage with Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) alumni on ways to increase their involvement in government discussions.
The Madani Government spokesman said the move followed Anwar’s recent meeting with UiTM alumni, which brought together many experienced individuals, including those from the corporate sector.
“The Prime Minister has instructed the Chief Secretary to engage with UiTM alumni to discuss ways they can become more involved, particularly in discussions involving certain ministries for the national interest.
“During his meeting with UiTM alumni, many of them demonstrated extensive experience, including in the corporate sector, and expressed their willingness to contribute to discussions and joint efforts with the government,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Johan Setia reports highest unhealthy API level at 166, twenty areas in total experiencing bad air
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Twenty areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4.30 pm today, with Johan Setia in Selangor registering the highest level at 166.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, four other areas in Selangor also recorded unhealthy air quality: Shah Alam (164), Klang (158), Petaling Jaya (155) and Banting (143).
Two monitoring stations in the capital recorded a similar trend, in Cheras (162) and Batu Muda (160), while Putrajaya registered 157.
In Johor, the affected areas were Pasir Gudang (164), Larkin (162), Kota Tinggi (155), Pengerang (152) and Kluang (110), while in Negeri Sembilan, they were Nilai (161) and Seremban (153).
Unhealthy readings were also recorded in Balok Baru and Indera Mahkota in Pahang, each at 156.
They were followed by Kuala Terengganu, Terengganu (154), Bandaraya Melaka, Melaka (125) and Kota Bharu, Kelantan (103).
Meanwhile, 45 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while only three were at a good level.
API readings of zero to 50 are categorised as good, 51 to 100 (moderate), 101 to 200 (unhealthy), 201 to 300 (very unhealthy) and above 300 (hazardous).  — Bernama

Title: Flying this weekend? Malaysia Airlines urges KLIA passengers to arrive early amid Sepang F1 traffic
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Malaysia Airlines advises passengers travelling from KL International Airport (KLIA) on Oct 2-4, 2026 to allow additional travel time to the airport, due to expected traffic congestion during the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit.

Title: Sarawak hydrogen market viability still unproven, says analyst
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Sept 30 — Putrajaya should think twice about extending incentives to Sarawak’s hydrogen sector when it has yet to prove that there are enough buyers willing to pay commercially viable prices, according to an analyst.
Samirul Ariff Othman from Global Asia Consulting said the concern was particularly relevant after Sarawak sought more Budget 2027 support for clean energy and other high-value industries, in a meeting this week between Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Awang Tengah Ali Hasan and Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
He said the basic problem with hydrogen was not Sarawak’s ability to produce it, but whether anyone wanted to buy enough of it at a price that made the business sustainable.
“You can build the plant and produce the hydrogen. But if you do not have customers willing to pay the price, you do not yet have a business. A production advantage matters only if enough of it survives delivery.”
The Energy Industries Council previously reported that Sarawak’s flagship export-oriented H2biscus and H2ornbill projects were scaled down following weak demand signals and uncertainty over securing buyers, while the state later acknowledged that the projects were also facing financial constraints.
The problem was particularly clear in the proposed Japanese market.
Sarawak Economic Development Corporation (SEDC) Energy chairman Tan Sri Abdul Aziz Husain said hydrogen could be produced in Sarawak for below RM20 per kg, but compression, cooling and transport pushed the delivered cost in Japan to around RM50 per kg. He said the original proposal to export all the hydrogen to Japan was therefore not viable unless support such as subsidies was provided in the buyer country.
Samirul said incentives made more sense where they helped an otherwise viable investment get across the line.
“If there is already a customer, an investor and a project that makes commercial sense, an incentive can help Malaysia win that investment. But if the market itself is not there yet, the government has to be much more careful because taxpayers are effectively taking the demand risk.”
As for domestic demand, Samirul noted that in August 2025, the Darul Hana hydrogen facility had a stated capacity of 150 kilogrammes a day and supplied ten fuel-cell vehicles. SEDC Energy’s chief executive acknowledged it was “uneconomical” to leave an operational plant underused.
According to Samirul, Sarawak is trying to boost domestic demand through publicly backed entities, specifically the Kuching Urban Transportation System. KUTS is expected to have around 38 hydrogen-powered ART vehicles and 55 hydrogen feeder buses.
“KUTS gives the hydrogen plant a buyer, but essentially the state is buying from itself,” he said.
“The state backs the producer, the state backs the transport operator and public money pays for the infrastructure. That may be useful to get the technology going, but it does not tell you whether other customers would choose hydrogen at that price.”
He added that this model also does not establish value for money.
“If a publicly backed producer sells hydrogen to a publicly backed transport operator, the financial assessment must cover both organisations. Revenue received by one may be expenditure supported by the state in another.”
Samirul said this did not mean Putrajaya should reject Sarawak’s request for clean-energy incentives altogether, such as in renewables.
“Some of these technologies and projects already have customers and proven economics. But for others, it would be better to see real buyers, binding offtake agreements and a clear idea of when the industry stops depending on the government to create demand before more support goes in.”
He added that even hydrogen, ammonia and methanol involve different processing requirements and markets. Each requires its own business case.
Returns on investment
Samirul said the wider question is how Sarawak converts resource wealth into lasting productive capacity. The 2026 state budget, for instance, allocated RM1 billion for ART infrastructure and systems.
“Sarawak receives substantial revenue from oil and gas, and that has given the state much more money to invest. So once you start putting that money into a new industry, the obvious question is: what are Sarawakians getting back?”
Samirul said emerging industries did not necessarily have to make an immediate profit, but governments should still be able to show why the investment was better than alternative uses of the same money.
“There has to be a credible path to a return. If the same ringgit could go into power, infrastructure or another industry where there are already customers waiting, then hydrogen has to show why it deserves that ringgit instead,” he added.
“Capital has alternative uses. So does electricity. Hydropower allocated to hydrogen could potentially serve other industries, households or electricity sales.”
He added that the evidence available supports disciplined experimentation and fuller disclosure.
“It does not establish that Sarawak’s hydrogen strategy has failed. Equally, strategic promise cannot substitute indefinitely for demonstrable results.”

Title: Immigration Dept denies social media claim that Myanmar teen was repatriated, says she remains in detention
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — The Immigration Department today denied claims that a Myanmar teenage girl was among those repatriated to Myanmar yesterday, saying she remains in custody at an immigration detention depot.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said checks by the department found that the teenager was not involved in the September 29 repatriation programme, which saw Myanmar nationals transported home aboard Myanmar naval vessels.
“Checks by the department confirmed that the individual remains detained at an Immigration depot and was not involved in the repatriation programme for Myanmar nationals via Myanmar military vessels yesterday,” he said in a statement.
The department said the clarification followed a viral social-media post alleging that the Myanmar teenager had been sent back under the programme, although it did not identify the account behind the post or provide further details about the girl.
The claim emerged as Malaysia yesterday began repatriating 1,476 Myanmar detainees from 14 immigration depots, comprising 1,370 men, 79 women, 20 boys and seven girls.
Zakaria said the department was aware of concerns over the safety and welfare of detainees, adding that humanitarian considerations were taken into account in enforcing immigration laws and procedures.
The department also said immigration depots were managed in accordance with the United Nations Standard Minimum Rules for the Treatment of Prisoners, or Nelson Mandela Rules, as well as domestic regulations governing immigration depots.
It urged the public not to circulate unverified information that could cause confusion over the department’s actions and procedures.

Title: Myanmar man gets 16 years’ prison for killing 80-year-old fruit seller in Taman OUG
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — A Myanmar man was sentenced to 16 years’ imprisonment by the High Court today after pleading guilty to causing the death of an elderly fruit seller at a house in Taman OUG, three years ago.
Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin handed down the sentence on Shofi Husson Fozo Rahman, 29, and ordered the accused to serve the prison term from the date of his arrest on Sept 26, 2023.
He was charged with causing the death of Ah Kau @ Yow Chow Chong, 80, at 6.30 pm on Sept 26, 2023, under Section 304(a) of the Penal Code, which provides for a maximum prison sentence of 30 years and a fine.
Based on the facts of the case, the victim had gone to the house to collect fruit for sale before an argument broke out between the two men. The accused then took a knife and stabbed the victim in the neck and body.
CCTV footage showed the victim at the scene before the accused approached him and threw an object believed to be a knife as he left the scene.
A post-mortem found that the victim had sustained six stab wounds, including two to the neck that penetrated muscle and major blood vessels, causing serious bleeding, as well as a wound to the left forearm.
Earlier, deputy public prosecutor Faridah Nurdinie Bahrum sought a deterrent sentence that would serve as a lesson to the accused and society at large.
“Although the victim was 80 years old, he was still working, and the scene was where he kept his fruit. He was a father, and his death had a profound impact on his family. As a foreign national, the accused should have complied with the laws of this country,” she said.
Meanwhile, the accused’s lawyer Datuk C. Vignesh Kumar sought a prison sentence of between 12 and 15 years, taking into account his client’s guilty plea, which spared the court’s time and costs
He added that his client has no prior criminal record and supports a wife and a child.
“The accused behaved well while in prison. His experience in prison has had a profound effect on him. He also apologises and is remorseful for his actions,” said the lawyer. — Bernama

Title: Primary Six pupil suffers burns after setting off firecrackers, Muar cops probe social media influence
Article:
MUAR, Sept 30 — A Primary Six pupil, believed to have been influenced by action and high-intensity content on social media, suffered burns after setting off firecrackers at a school here yesterday.
The incident also triggered panic among parents and the school community.
Muar police chief Assistant Commissioner Raiz Mukhliz Azman Aziz said the 12-year-old boy was injured in the incident, which occurred at about 11am.
“The pupil involved was then taken to Sultanah Fatimah Specialist Hospital (HPSF) here for treatment.
“A preliminary psychiatric assessment was also conducted on the pupil before he was allowed to continue treatment as an outpatient.
“Examinations revealed that the victim suffered burns on several parts of his body and is currently receiving treatment,” he said in a statement today.
Raiz Mukhliz said initial investigations later led police to detain the pupil to assist in the probe.
He said investigations suggested the pupil was likely influenced by action and high-intensity content on social media and the internet.
“However, further investigations are being conducted to identify all the factors that led to the incident.
“A search was also conducted at the scene and the pupil’s residence where several items believed to be linked to the incident were seized for further investigation and analysis,” he said.
Raiz Mukhliz said six witnesses had come forward to assist investigators, while efforts to locate other witnesses were ongoing.
He said the school acted proactively immediately after the incident by directing pupils to a safe area before seeking police assistance.
A safety inspection was also carried out at the scene by the Muar district police bomb disposal unit, while the Johor police contingent’s forensic unit conducted a forensic examination.
“Checks and inspections found no other explosive threats in the vicinity of the incident,” he said.
Earlier, the pupil was brought before the Magistrate's Court, where police obtained a four-day remand order until Saturday to facilitate investigations.
The case is being investigated under Section 436 of the Penal Code for mischief by fire or explosive substance with intent to damage, as well as Sections 6 and 8 of the Explosives Act 1957.
